get.summary: list ducklakes
list declared measures and dimensions on DuckLake tables
get.description: Call this before writing any aggregate query over a DuckLake table. A declared measure is the canonical definition of that number, and reproducing it yourself will silently disagree with it (a `revenue` measure typically excludes refunds or test rows). Filter by `table` for one table's declarations, or by `path_prefix` (e.g. `f/analytics`) for everything declared under a folder; omit both to browse the whole catalog. Results are keyset-paged: a full page may mean more remain, so continue with the `cursor_*` params rather than assuming a measure does not exist. Use each returned `expr` verbatim, and when a measure has a `filter` write it as `expr FILTER (WHERE filter)` so measures with different predicates can share one GROUP BY. If a number you need has no declared measure, write your own aggregate as usual. Results are limited to declarations whose producing script the caller can read.

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: DuckLake table path, with or without the `ducklake://` scheme

parameters.name: path_prefix
parameters.description: Producing script path prefix, e.g. `f/analytics`

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Results per page, capped at 1000 (default 1000)

parameters.name: cursor_table
parameters.description: Keyset cursor. To page, pass the previous response's `next_cursor` fields back as `cursor_*`; all four move together, and are omitted for the first page. Continue whenever `next_cursor` is present. Every returned row is one the caller may read, so the cursor never names a hidden row.

Re-read where a guest session is minted and at the auth door on every guest request, so turning it off takes effect immediately, for sessions already issued and for apps whose policy already says `guest`. post.summary: set the key guest JWTs are verified against for this workspace
post.description: A guest JWT (`jwt_guest_`) is minted by the embedding customer's own backend and verified against this key: a PEM public key (RS/ES family, HS* refused) or a JWKS URL, at most one. Both empty clears the workspace key; off cloud, verification then falls back to the instance issuer (`JWT_EXT_JWKS_URL`) if one is set, else no guest JWT is accepted (`guest_access_enabled` is the on/off switch). Workspace-admin gated. The key is validated before it is stored. Setting a key is refused with a 400 where guests are unavailable (the shared cloud); clearing one always works.

Creates a new script at a path that does not already hold one.
Supplying `parent_hash` instead deploys a new version of the script that hash names, and a `path` differing from that version's moves the script there. `POST /w/{workspace}/scripts/update/{path}` does the same, naming the superseded version in its URL.
post.x-mcp-tool-description: Creates a script at a path that does not already hold one.
post.x-mcp-instructions: Specify the path (e.g., 'f/my_folder/my_script'), the content (source code), and the language. For TypeScript, use 'bun' unless deno-specific APIs are needed. A path that already holds a script is refused: use updateScript to deploy a new version of it, and do NOT delete and recreate a script to change it. A new version generates its lock async, and only a version with a lock is runnable: until it lands, a run by path still executes the previous version. Poll getScriptByPath before running the new one and stop on either outcome: lock non-null means it is ready, lock_error_logs set means the lockfile failed and that version will never run, so report the error instead of polling on.

post.description:
Deploys a new version of the script at `path`, which must already hold one.
The body's `path` is the destination: the same path leaves the script where it
is, a different one moves it there and archives the old path.

requestBody.description: The new version of the script, whose `path` is where it should end up.

post.x-mcp-instructions: Deploys a new version of an existing script, preserving its history, so do NOT delete and recreate a script to change it. Send the whole script, not a patch: read the current one with getScriptByPath first, unless you wrote its content yourself. Set path__body only to move the script to a different path; omit it to leave the script where it is. A path that holds no script is refused: use createScript to create one. A new version generates its lock async, and only a version with a lock is runnable: until it lands, a run by path still executes the previous version. Poll getScriptByPath before running the new one and stop on either outcome: lock non-null means it is ready, lock_error_logs set means the lockfile failed and that version will never run, so report the error instead of polling on.

post.description:
Moves the start of a queued job that is waiting for a future time (scheduled, debounced,
re-scheduled by a concurrency limit, or a flow step waiting on a sleep or a retry delay)
to now, keeping the same job id. A job with a
concurrency limit is still checked against its limit when it is pulled. A schedule's
upcoming tick is refused, since the schedule would queue that tick again.

get.summary: Column-level lineage of a set of dbt relations
get.description:
The direct (`copy` / `mod`) column-to-column lineage the given relations' columns sit in — the connected component around them, from the engine's static analysis. Not their own edges, which would stop one hop out since a column trace walks transitively, and not a whole project's, which carries model families the selection cannot reach.
Several relations, answered as one union, because one selection reaches several: a script's output column can derive from columns of several dbt models. Unpinned, the component crosses projects — a relation one project produces is another's source — and the caller's access is decided again for every project it reaches, so a trace ends where their grants do. A pinned answer, by version here or by job on the run route, is one project's.
Its own endpoint rather than a field on the asset graph: the graph is folder-wide and polled by a run page, while this is rendered for one selection at a time. Empty for projects that did not opt into the analysis pass (`column_lineage: true`), which is the ordinary case. The indirect `scan` kind is stored but never served: it reaches every output column of its model.

parameters.name: asset_path
parameters.description: The `dbt://` relations whose lineage to return. Repeated, once per relation, and answered as one union. At least one, and at most 1000 — a request naming none, or more than that, is refused rather than answered with an empty component.

parameters.name: dbt_script_hash
parameters.description:
The deployed version a view is drawing, when it is drawing one — the dbt editor, which shows a single project as of a single deploy. A version-pinned answer is that version's project alone, the same as a job-pinned one, and only the unpinned answer crosses projects: a pin says which stored graph is on screen, and another project's live graph is not part of it.
A run's or an editor buffer's own graph is not reachable here: that pins to a job, and costs the job-read gate — see `jobs/dbt_column_lineage/{id}`.

One project answers here, the one the run is of, since the graph this annotates is that project's too. Authorized through the job, the same gate as `dbt_graph`. macro_edges.description: Macro-library → consumer edges (deploy-recorded call detection plus `// use`). Omitted when empty.

test_edges.description: Ordering-only "must-run-after" edges — a `// data_test relationships` (or custom test reading a pipeline asset) requires the referenced asset's producer to run before the tested script. Not a data-consumption edge; fed into the cascade topo-sort so cold runs order correctly. Omitted when empty.

dbt_edges.description: `ref()` lineage BETWEEN two dbt models, in the terms the canvas draws — the relations, not dbt's node ids. Without it every model hangs off the one dbt runnable and the project reads as a flat fan-out. Omitted when empty.

dbt_snapshot_job.description: The job whose own snapshot the dbt half was resolved from, when one was asked for and found. A run page polls the graph while its job runs, because a dynamic descriptor's snapshot is written mid-run, and this is what tells it to stop. Omitted when the answer came from the version's deployed graph.

dbt_graph_ingested_at.description: When the dbt half on screen was parsed, for a graph pinned to a job. What the dbt editor labels its provenance with — "parsed from the editor at 14:32" against "as of last deploy" — since the two are drawn identically and the ambiguity would otherwise just move into the editor. Omitted for the unpinned workspace graph, which spans every project and so has no one time.

truncated.description: The component reaches further than `edges`, which holds the part nearest the asked-for relations. A trace that stops short is otherwise indistinguishable from one that ends.

DbtColumnLineage.description: The direct column-to-column lineage the asked-for relations' columns sit in — the connected component around them — in the terms the canvas draws: relations and columns, never dbt's node ids.

materialize_strategy.description: The Windmill write strategy it maps to, absent for `view` and `ephemeral`, which have none.

column_schema.description: Every column of the relation, typed and in the order the model produces them, from the engine's static analysis. Present only for a project that opted into it, and gated like `columns` and the model's SQL: a full column list is the shape of what the author wrote.

raw_code.description: The model's SQL as written, at the deploy this graph belongs to. Omitted when the caller cannot read the script.

original_file_path.description: Its path inside the dbt project, e.g. `models/staging/stg_orders.sql`.

DbtAssetProvenance.description: What dbt says about the model, snapshot, seed or source that produces (or, for a source, is read at) this relation. A dbt project is one runnable node with many model assets, so per-model metadata belongs here rather than on the script.

draft_base.description:
The deployed version the draft forked from, as text whatever the
kind (script hash, flow version id, app version id). Compare to the
deployed head to tell a draft that is behind. Absent when there is
no draft or it was never forked from a deploy.

other_drafts_users.description:
Other workspace users (and the legacy NULL-email row, if any)
with a saved draft at the same path. Populated only on the
authed user's "get by path" responses for kinds the editor
surfaces a fork banner for (script, flow, app, raw_app).
Empty / omitted for kinds without that UI.

UserDraftOverlay.description:
Overlay fields added to every "get by path" response that accepts
the `get_draft` query parameter. The deployed payload is sent
untouched in the response body; the authed user's saved draft
for this path — whatever shape the editor wrote — is attached
as the sibling `draft` field when `get_draft=true` and a draft
exists. The frontend pairs the two to present diff / reset /
discard UI; the server never merges them.

When `no_deployed=true` there is no deployed row at this path —
the response body is a best-effort stand-in synthesized from
the draft, and only `draft` is canonical. Callers should disable
"diff vs deployed" UI in that case.

UserDraftItemKind.description:
Closed set of item kinds a user can autosave as a draft. Mirrors the
Postgres `DRAFT_KIND` enum and the backend `UserDraftItemKind`.

summary.description: Short description of what this flow does

description.description: Detailed documentation for this flow

on_behalf_of_email.description: Address of the account the flow runs on behalf of. Derived from on_behalf_of on read; accepted on write, where it is resolved to the account it names.

on_behalf_of.description: The flow runs with the permissions of this identity: u/{username}, g/{group}, or a bare email when the username is itself email-shaped. The only stored half of the identity; on_behalf_of_email is derived from it. Omit it when writing and it is resolved from that address instead.

OpenFlow.description: Top-level flow definition containing metadata, configuration, and the flow structure

modules.description: Array of steps that execute in sequence. Each step can be a script, subflow, loop, or branch

same_worker.description: If true, all steps run on the same worker for better performance

preserve_step_tags.description: If true and the flow runs on a custom worker tag, steps that declare their own non-empty tag run on it instead of inheriting the flow tag. Steps without their own tag still inherit the flow tag.

concurrent_limit.description: Maximum number of concurrent executions of this flow

concurrency_key.description: Expression to group concurrent executions (e.g., by user ID)

concurrency_time_window_s.description: Time window in seconds for concurrent_limit

debounce_delay_s.description: Delay in seconds to debounce flow executions

debounce_key.description: Expression to group debounced executions

debounce_args_to_accumulate.description: Arguments to accumulate across debounced executions

max_total_debouncing_time.description: Maximum total time in seconds that a job can be debounced

max_total_debounces_amount.description: Maximum number of times a job can be debounced

skip_expr.description: JavaScript expression to conditionally skip the entire flow

cache_ttl.description: Cache duration in seconds for flow results

delete_after_secs.description: If set, delete the flow job's args, result and logs after this many seconds following job completion

priority.description: Execution priority (higher numbers run first)

early_return.description: Id of the step whose result a sync webhook returns as soon as that step completes, while the rest of the flow keeps running. When the step does not run, or fails while the flow has a failure module, the flow's final result is returned instead.

chat_input_enabled.description: Whether this flow accepts chat-style input

notes.description: Sticky notes attached to the flow

groups.description: Semantic groups of modules for organizational purposes

FlowValue.description: The flow structure containing modules and optional preprocessor/failure handlers

Retry.description: Retry configuration for failed module executions

skip_if_stopped.description: If true, following steps are skipped when this condition triggers

expr.description: JavaScript expression evaluated after the module runs. Can use 'result' (step's result) or 'flow_input'. Return true to stop

error_message.description: Custom error message when stopping with an error. Mutually exclusive with skip_if_stopped. If set to a non-empty string, the flow stops with this error. If empty string, a default error message is used. If null or omitted, no error is raised.

error_include_result.description: When stopping with an error (error_message set), embed the stopping step's own result inside the raised error object (as error.result) instead of discarding it. The top-level result stays { error }. Defaults to false.

StopAfterIf.description: Early termination condition for a module

id.description: Unique identifier for this step. Used to reference results via 'results.step_id'. Must be a valid identifier (alphanumeric, underscore, hyphen)

cache_ttl.description: Cache duration in seconds for this step's results

delete_after_secs.description: If set, delete the step's args, result and logs after this many seconds following job completion

summary.description: Short description of what this step does

priority.description: Execution priority for this step (higher numbers run first)

continue_on_error.description: If true, flow continues even if this step fails

job_token_scopes.description: Scopes the token of this step's jobs is restricted to (domain:action[:resource], e.g. oidc:write), on top of the flow's own restriction: a step can only narrow it. Applies to everything the step runs (loop and branch bodies, AI agent tools).

FlowModule.description: A single step in a flow. Can be a script, subflow, loop, or branch

InputTransform.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

value.description: The static value. For resources, use format '$res:path/to/resource'

StaticTransform.description: Static value passed directly to the step. Use for hardcoded values or resource references like '$res:path/to/resource'

expr.description: JavaScript expression returning the value. Available variables - results (object with all previous step results), flow_input (flow inputs), flow_input.iter (in loops)

JavascriptTransform.description: JavaScript expression evaluated at runtime. Can reference previous step results via 'results.step_id' or flow inputs via 'flow_input.property'. Inside for loops, use 'flow_input.iter.value' for the current iteration value (in while loops it equals 'flow_input.iter.index')

AiTransform.description: Value resolved by the AI runtime for this input. The AI engine decides how to satisfy the parameter.

resource.description: Resource reference in format '$res:{resource_path}' pointing to provider credentials

reasoning_effort.description: Provider-native reasoning effort token (e.g. 'low', 'high', 'none') for models that support extended thinking. Optional; unset leaves the provider default.

ProviderConfig.description: Complete AI provider configuration with resource reference and model selection

ProviderTransform.description: Provider configuration - can be static (ProviderConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

MemoryConfig.description: Managed memory, stored by Windmill and replayed with each request. The memory is named by a memory id, see `memory_id`. While it is off, a step can supply its history in `previous_messages`.

FlowModuleValue.description: The actual implementation of a flow step. Can be a script (inline or referenced), subflow, loop, branch, or special module type

content.description: The script source code. Should export a 'main' function

path.description: Optional path for saving this script

tag.description: Worker group tag for execution routing

concurrent_limit.description: Maximum concurrent executions of this script

custom_concurrency_key.description: Custom key for grouping concurrent executions

is_trigger.description: If true, this script is a trigger that can start the flow

assets.description: External resources this script accesses (S3 objects, resources, etc.)

RawScript.description: Inline script with code defined directly in the flow. Use 'bun' as default language if unspecified. The script receives arguments from input_transforms

path.description: Path to the script in the workspace (e.g., 'f/scripts/send_email')

hash.description: Optional specific version hash of the script to use

tag_override.description: Override the script's default worker group tag

is_trigger.description: If true, this script is a trigger that can start the flow

PathScript.description: Reference to an existing script by path. Use this when calling a previously saved script instead of writing inline code

path.description: Path to the flow in the workspace (e.g., 'f/flows/process_user')

PathFlow.description: Reference to an existing flow by path. Use this to call another flow as a subflow

modules.description: Steps to execute for each iteration. These can reference the iteration value via 'flow_input.iter.value'

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (faster for I/O-bound operations). Use with parallelism to control concurrency

ForloopFlow.description: Executes nested modules in a loop over an iterator. Inside the loop, use 'flow_input.iter.value' to access the current iteration value, and 'flow_input.iter.index' for the index. Supports parallel execution for better performance on I/O-bound operations

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (use with caution in while loops)

WhileloopFlow.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

branches.description: Array of branches to evaluate in order. The first branch with expr evaluating to true executes

default.description: Steps to execute if no branch expressions match

BranchOne.description: Conditional branching where only the first matching branch executes. Branches are evaluated in order, and the first one with a true expression runs. If no branches match, the default branch executes

branches.description: Array of branches that all execute (either in parallel or sequentially)

parallel.description: If true, all branches execute concurrently. If false, they execute sequentially

BranchAll.description: Parallel branching where all branches execute simultaneously. Unlike BranchOne, all branches run regardless of conditions. Useful for executing independent tasks concurrently

tools.description: Array of tools the agent can use. The agent decides which tools to call based on the task

tag.description: Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the AI agent step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)

omit_output_from_conversation.description: If true, this AI agent step does not persist its assistant or tool messages to the flow conversation when chat mode is enabled.

agent.description:
Path of a reusable `ai_agent` resource (hybrid linking). When set, the agent brain
config (provider/model/system prompt/etc.) and tool set are resolved at runtime from
that resource; the module's input_transforms then only carry the flow-local inputs
(user_message, user_attachments, enabled_tools and the history inputs memory_id and previous_messages)
and, optionally, the `model` and `reasoning_effort` overrides of what the agent saved.

parallel.description: If true, the agent can execute multiple tool calls in parallel

AiAgent.description: AI agent step that can use tools to accomplish tasks. The agent receives inputs and can call any of its configured tools to complete the task

tag.description: Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)

AiDecision.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

flow.description: If true, marks this as a flow identity (special handling)

Identity.description: Pass-through module that returns its input unchanged. Useful for flow structure or as a placeholder

id.description: Unique identifier for the note

color.description: Color of the note, one of: yellow, blue, green, purple, pink, orange, red, cyan, lime, gray. Any other value renders unstyled.

locked.description: Whether the note is locked and cannot be edited or moved

contained_node_ids.description: For group notes, the IDs of nodes contained within this group

FlowNote.description: A sticky note attached to a flow for documentation and annotation

checked_at.description: Timestamp when the health check was actually performed (not cache return time)

workers_alive.description: Number of workers that pinged within last 5 minutes

checked_at.description: Timestamp when the health check was performed

DetailedHealthResponse.description: Detailed health status response (always fresh, no caching)

size.description: Current number of connections in the pool

active_count.description: Number of active workers (pinged in last 5 minutes)

pending_jobs.description: Number of pending jobs in the queue

healthy.description: Whether the server is ready to accept requests

operator.description: If true, auto-invited users are added as operators. If false, they are added as developers.

AutoInviteConfig.description: Configuration for auto-inviting users to the workspace

path.description: Path to the error handler script or flow

ErrorHandlerConfig.description: Configuration for the workspace error handler

path.description: Path to the success handler script or flow

SuccessHandlerConfig.description: Configuration for the workspace success handler

EditErrorHandlerBody.description: Request body for editing the workspace error handler. Accepts both new grouped format and legacy flat format for backward compatibility.

path.description: Path to the error handler script or flow

fallback_to_instance_alerts.description: Report failed jobs to the instance critical alert channels when no workspace error handler is set. Omit to leave the stored value untouched.

EditErrorHandlerNew.description: New grouped format for editing error handler

error_handler.description: Path to the error handler script or flow

EditErrorHandlerLegacy.description: Legacy flat format for editing error handler (deprecated, use new format)

path.description: Path to the variable expiration handler script or flow

muted_on_user_path.description: Do not run the handler for variables on a personal (u/) path

notify_before_secs.description: How long before a variable's value expires the handler runs. 1 day when omitted.

remind_every_secs.description: Run the handler again at this interval until the value expires. No reminders when omitted or 0.

EditVariableExpirationHandlerBody.description: Request body for editing the workspace variable expiration handler. Omit `path` (or send null) to unset the handler.

EditSuccessHandlerBody.description: Request body for editing the workspace success handler. Accepts both new grouped format and legacy flat format for backward compatibility.

path.description: Path to the success handler script or flow

EditSuccessHandlerNew.description: New grouped format for editing success handler

success_handler.description: Path to the success handler script or flow

EditSuccessHandlerLegacy.description: Legacy flat format for editing success handler (deprecated, use new format)

mount_path.description: KV v2 secrets engine mount path (e.g., windmill)

kv_secret_path_prefix.description: Optional path prefix inserted between the KV data/metadata segment and the workspace id (e.g., "apps/windmill"). When set, secrets are stored at `<mount>/data/<prefix>/<workspace>/<secret>`, allowing a Vault policy scoped to exactly `<mount>/data/<prefix>/*`.

jwt_role.description: Vault JWT auth role name for Windmill (optional, if not provided token auth is used)

jwt_mount_path.description: Mount path for the JWT auth method in Vault (optional, defaults to "jwt"). Set this when the JWT auth method is mounted at a non-default path, e.g. via `vault auth enable -path=<mount> jwt`.

token.description: Static Vault token for testing/development (optional, if provided this is used instead of JWT authentication)

skip_ssl_verify.description: Skip TLS certificate verification when connecting to Vault. Only use for self-signed certificates in development environments.

client_secret.description: Azure AD client secret. Optional — when omitted, the integration falls back to Azure Workload Identity Federation, exchanging the Kubernetes-projected service-account JWT at AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE for an access token (no long-lived secret stored).

token.description: Static Bearer token for testing/development (optional, if provided this is used instead of OAuth2 authentication)

access_key_id.description: AWS Access Key ID (optional, uses default credential chain if not provided)

endpoint_url.description: Custom endpoint URL for testing (e.g., LocalStack)

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID where the secret is located

path.description: Path of the secret that failed to migrate

error.description: Error message

failed_count.description: Number of secrets that failed to migrate

failures.description: Details of any failures encountered during migration

keys.description: Array of JSON Web Keys for JWT verification

path.description: Path of the ai_agent resource.

version.description: The agent's per-path version number when the run opened: how many times the resource had been saved, not a resource_version row id. For `agent` and `agent_draft` it names the configuration the run read and every case executed. For `agent_version` it is the request's own, says which version to inline, and is required.

draft_hash.description: Hash of the configuration a draft run executed, stamped server-side. A draft moves without the version moving, so this is what dates a run of one. It is also what recognises a draft run whose configuration was later deployed: when it matches the agent as deployed, the run's kind and version are rewritten to that version, once, and the hash is kept as what the resolution rests on.

EvalSubject.description: What an eval run is executed against.

AgentDraft.description: The brain and tools of an agent, as the flow editor holds them. Carried by the request and present exactly when the subject kind is `agent_draft` — the edits exist only in the editor — where it is the whole definition of what ran: the run goes through the same unlinked branch of the agent executor the editor's own test uses.

scorers.description: The columns of the results table, in display order.

EvalCaseInput.description: The inputs a standalone run feeds the agent.

expected.description: Reference output a scorer compares a rerun against.

id.description: Absent for a case the dataset does not hold yet.

expected.description: Reference output a scorer compares a rerun against.
Reference output a scorer compares a rerun against.

name.description: Column header. Defaults to the last segment of the path.

pass_if.description: A score at or above this counts as a pass, and the column reports a pass rate beside its mean. Applied when results are read rather than when they are produced, so moving the line re-reads every score already recorded instead of invalidating them.

path.description: The script, or the ai_agent resource used as a judge.

Scorer.description: A scorer is a column of the results table, and it is always a runnable: an ai_agent resource sent the run to grade, or a script handed the run as an argument. `id` is assigned when the scorer is added to a dataset and never reused: it is what makes a column the same column across experiments when the scorer is renamed, and a delta is only ever computed between two scores carrying the same id. A scorer sent without an id is given one.

run_number.description: This agent's nth run of this dataset, allocated once and never reused. What a run is called. Numbered per agent rather than per subject kind: runs of what is deployed and runs of its draft are the same agent's history.

run_job_id.description: The flow executing the run: one job holding every case and its scores.

scores.description: What the run scored, one entry per scorer that produced a number. Carried on the run itself so a list of runs can say what each one scored without reading every cell of every one of them. Empty on a run whose scores have not been read yet.

running.description: Whether the flow executing this run is still going. What makes a list of runs worth watching rather than worth reloading.

EvalExperiment.description: One run of a dataset: written once when the dataset is run, and only ever read afterwards. The case set it executed is returned by the results endpoint, not here: a listing would otherwise send the whole dataset back once per experiment.

name.description: What the column is called in the dataset that ran it, resolved server-side because a list of runs spanning datasets cannot hold every dataset's scorers to look it up.

pass_rate.description: The share of scored cells at or above the column's threshold, for a column that has one. Absent where the column has no threshold and the mean is the whole headline.

failed.description: How many of the run's cells the column failed on. A column that failed on all of them has no number to report and is still one of the columns that ran.

ExperimentScore.description: One scorer's headline for one run: the two numbers a column reports, over that run's cells.

not_applicable.description: The scorer read this case and had nothing to measure on it. Left out of the column's mean and pass rate rather than counted as a zero.

pending.description: A scoring job is still running for this cell.

passed.description: Which side of the scorer's `pass_if` threshold the score fell on. Absent when the column has no threshold, or has no score yet.

baseline.description: The same scorer's number on the baseline experiment.

definition_changed.description: The baseline's score came from a different definition of this scorer, so the delta is a change of scorer as much as a change of agent.

CellScore.description: One scorer's verdict on one run, and how it compares with the baseline.

job_id.description: The iteration that ran this case. Absent between a run being recorded and its flow reaching this case, which reads as a case still to run.

output.description: The agent's answer. The full trajectory stays reachable through job_id.

subject_version.description: The agent version this cell ran against. Cells of one experiment can differ, which the table says rather than averaging two versions silently.

subject_draft_hash.description: For a run of unsaved edits, the hash of the configuration this cell ran. Edits move without a version changing, so this is what identifies what ran, and what recognises a run whose edits were later saved as a run of that version.

scores.description: One entry per scorer of the dataset, in column order.

pass_rate.description: The share of scored cells that passed, for a column with a threshold. Reported beside the mean rather than instead of it: a pass rate says how many cases are good enough, a mean says by how much, and neither answers the other's question.

missing_in_baseline.description: Cells the baseline has no score for, so a column the baseline never ran shows as unscored rather than as a spurious difference.

ScorerMean.description: A column's summary. There is no single number for a dataset: averaging a judge with an exact match would invent one.

tool_arguments.description: On a tool row, the arguments the model wrote for the call. For a script, flow or AI agent tool these exclude the inputs its step wires in, which only the tool's job holds. Null for a provider-native web search, whose query the provider does not return.

tool_result.description: On a tool row, the text the model got back from the call, or what the call failed with — the row's own text names the tool rather than the reason. For a provider-native web search, its citations.

reasoning.description: On an answer, the thinking that produced it; on a tool row, the thinking that led to the call. Each round's thinking is on one row. The agent job's result keeps the turn's thinking as a single string.

attachments.description: The files a user message carried, as object-storage references: every flow input other than user_message that held one or a list of them, at most 20. Never file bytes or a presigned URL.

description.description: Short description of the tool

instructions.description: Detailed instructions for using the tool

path.description: API endpoint path

copilot_disabled.description: Hides the Windmill AI assistant (chat, sessions, code generation, completion, fixes) from the workspace UI. Read from the workspace's own settings even when the providers served fall back to the instance config. AI agent steps and the AI sandbox in flows are unaffected.

sessions_storage_disabled.description: Stops browsers from backing their AI sessions up to the workspace's object storage. Read from the workspace's own settings like `copilot_disabled`.

sessions_retention_days.description: The server deletes the backup of a session no push has reached for this many days. Unset keeps backups until the user deletes the session. Read from the workspace's own settings like `copilot_disabled`.

epoch.description: the session's move count when this copy was pushed; of a session two workspaces list, the copy with the higher one is the later

listing.description: a fingerprint of the session's listing; pages of one session whose fingerprints differ do not belong together

moved.description: the backup kept changing while this page was read, so it may mix two versions; the browser starts the session over

AiSessionBackupCursor.description: where a pull of a session that did not fit one answer whole picks up; the rest of the session follows a pull naming that session alone with this as `resume`

partial.description: more parts of this session follow, in this push or a later one; the session is not listed on this one. Such a part names its push (`push`), or it is refused

whole.description: a part of a push of the session whole; the head is on the part that opens it, which replaces whatever the storage holds of the session, and every piece the browser has is on one of them. An incremental part instead rides on a session the storage lists and is refused with needs_whole when it lists none

push.description: a push split over several parts names itself on each with a token the browser draws; the part that opens it unlists the session and the last part lists it again, and a later part is written only while that token is the one there (refused with needs_whole otherwise)

opens.description: this part opens the push named by `push`

epoch.description: the session's move count (its record's `moves`), kept with the marker that lists the session; an incremental part rides on the marker of the same count

exhausted.description: The one-time grant is spent; no provider is served and the user must add their own API key.

used_ratio.description: Fraction of the grant consumed, 0 to 1.

FreeTierInfo.description: Read-only. Present when the workspace has no AI provider of its own and is running on Windmill's free tier. Ignored on write.

ModelPriceOverride.description: negotiated rates in USD per million tokens, keyed `provider:model`

reported_cost_nano_usd.description: only set by providers that bill back an exact figure

key.description: the grouped dimension's value; empty when grouping by model

hash.description: script version hash as a 16-char hex string

chat_input_enabled.description: flow-only. `chat_input_enabled` of the flow's value, projected so the list can mark flows that open as a chat. Omitted when the value has no such field.

ws_specific.description: agent-only. Whether the agent is workspace-specific, which keeps it out of deploys to other workspaces.

RunnableItem.description:
A row in the merged runnables listing. `type` is the discriminator;
kind-specific fields (hash/language/kind for scripts, execution_mode/
version for apps, agent_memory/ws_specific for agents) are present only
for that kind. An agent is an `ai_agent` resource whose description is
reported as `summary`. `edited_at` is the unified last-updated time (a
script's created_at, a flow/app/agent's edit time).

allowed_origins.description: Origins allowed to call this route cross-origin, matched against the request's Origin header (ignoring case) and echoed back on a match. When set, the list governs both the preflight and the response, overriding any Access-Control-Allow-Origin the runnable returns via wm_headers. Use ['*'] to opt out of any restriction, including the http_route_default_allowed_origins instance setting. An empty list is not a configuration and resolves exactly as null does. When null, the instance setting applies, or Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * if it is unset. Ignored on a static website, which has no authentication of its own and so hands out public files: restricting which browsers may read them protects nothing while breaking cross-origin webfonts and fetches. A single-file static asset is not exempt, since it can carry an authentication_method.

DatatableRoleCluster.description: The Windmill-managed Postgres cluster a data table role is a login on: Windmill's own (behind `instance` data tables) or the external instance cluster (behind `external_instance` ones). Defaults to `instance`.

in_use.description: Whether any data table, in any workspace, lets someone connect as this role. Only set in a data table's available_roles.

supported.description: Whether this data table can be put under roles at all. Only one on a database Windmill manages can: a role is a login on that database's cluster.

default_role.description: A role id, `admin`, or `$none` when the data table has no default role.

AclTarget.description: what access is read or changed on

AclChange.description: one change to plan or apply

role.description: a data table role of the instance, or admin

AclChangeSetOwner.description: hands the target to role — for a schema, with everything already in it but an extension's members, which stay with the extension

role.description: a data table role of the instance, or admin
a data table role of the instance, other than admin

objects.description: objects inside the target the revoke covers, empty for the target itself. Only with the target scope; a revoke on all objects of a kind is refused, since it cannot say which grants it takes back.

statements.description: The statements the plan showed. Required to apply, which plans again and refuses if the result differs.

kind.description: TABLE, SEQUENCE, FUNCTION, PROCEDURE or TYPE — what the object is. A revoke turns it into the keyword it takes, ROUTINE for both routine kinds; a type's grants are read only.

args.description: identity arguments of a routine, which is what tells two of the same name apart

future.description: set for a default privilege, naming the kind of object it covers (TABLES, SEQUENCES, FUNCTIONS, TYPES, or SCHEMAS). On a schema, the defaults set in that schema; on the database, the ones set database-wide, which apply in every schema and which no schema's own defaults take back.

sources.description: the roles the grant comes from, each once — who granted it, or for a default privilege the role whose future objects it covers. A revoke of some of the grant's privileges takes them back from every source that gave them.

privileges.description: what role gave of the grant's privileges. A revoke is held back only by a source out of reach that gave some of what it takes back.

reachable.description: whether the data table's connection can take back what role gave. On an object that is the owner, when the connection acts for the owner, and otherwise the connection itself; for a default privilege, a creating role the connection acts for. What a source out of reach gave is not revocable from here; privileges only other sources gave still are.

roles.description: the roles a change may name; empty unless the caller may change anything

editable.description: whether the caller may plan and apply changes

clone.description: whether this is a clone, whose grants stay as they were copied

supports_maintain.description: whether the server is Postgres 17+, which added the MAINTAIN table privilege

dbname.description: the database the target lives in

children.description: a database's schemas, or a schema's tables

error.description: Error message if the operation failed

used_by_workspaces.description: Workspaces that reference this database through a ducklake catalog or a datatable database of the kind being listed — 'instance' for the instance databases endpoint, 'external_instance' for the external cluster one. Computed at request time, not persisted, and only returned to superadmins.

workspace_id.description: The workspace a member created this database for as a fork copy. Only that workspace can import into it or point a fork at it.

memory_sample_count.description: number of jobs that have a peak memory reading

draining.description: the worker received its shutdown signal and exits once its current job is done

error_handler_fallback_to_instance_alert.description: Report failed jobs to the instance critical alert channels when no workspace error handler is set. Not available on cloud or on fork workspaces.

shared_ducklakes.description: Lake names the fork SHARES with the parent (reads and writes the parent's lake directly). Every lake not listed gets the default isolated fork namespace with read-defer to the parent.

shared_storages.description: Workspace storages the fork SHARES with the parent (`_default_` for the primary one): it reads and writes the parent's objects directly. Every storage not listed is isolated: the fork writes under its own prefix and reads through to the parent's objects.

is_dev_workspace.description: Create the fork as a persistent dev workspace (id not required to carry the wm-fork- prefix; at most one per parent)

lock_prod_deploy.description: When creating a dev workspace, lock the parent (prod) against direct deployment

lock_prod_forking.description: When creating a dev workspace, prevent forking the parent (prod)

copy_members.description: Copy the parent's members (users + group memberships) into the fork so the team can work in it

dev_workspace_label.description: Environment label of the dev workspace, e.g. 'dev' or 'staging'; null defaults to 'dev'

role.description: The workspace role the invite grants.

is_workspace_admin.description: Populated only for service accounts. True if the service account has workspace admin in its (single) workspace.

branch_or_iteration_n.description: 0-based iteration index for ForLoop / branch index for BranchAll. Iterations 0..n-1 are preserved; iteration n is restarted.

on_behalf_of.description: The user or group the app runs as in anonymous or publisher mode (e.g. 'u/admin' or 'g/mygroup'). The authority for the app's identity.

on_behalf_of_email.description: Address of `on_behalf_of`, written through from it on every save and returned as stored. Optional; when absent it is derived from `on_behalf_of`. Sending it is optional too; it must name the same account as `on_behalf_of`, and a pair that disagrees is rejected.

sandbox.description: Publisher opt-in to app sandbox isolation (alpha). When true the app is isolated from each viewer's Windmill session. When false/absent the app runs same-origin with the viewer's full session (the default, pre-isolation behavior).

frontend_sdk_scopes.description: Raw apps: author-declared scopes for the frontend SDK token. Takes effect only when `sandbox` is also true — an unsandboxed bundle runs with the viewer's own session, so no token is advertised or minted for it and this list stays inert. On a sandboxed app a non-empty list lets viewers mint (after consenting) a short-lived token carrying their own identity restricted to these scopes, handed to the app bundle so `windmill-client` calls run as the viewer. Must be a subset of the server's curated allowlist (jobs:run, jobs:read, users:read, resources:read, variables:read, flow_conversations:read, flow_conversations:write). Every such token can call whoami without consent, whether `users:read` is declared or not.

is_draft.description:
True when the authed user has a draft for this app — either no
deployed row exists at this path (draft-only) or the user has
saved a per-user draft on top of the deployed row.

draft_only.description: No deployed counterpart exists at this path — the draft is the whole item.

draft_path.description:
User-typed path the editor has staged but not yet deployed.
Sourced from the draft JSON's `draft_path` field (the editor
only writes it when the typed path differs from the deployed
one). Lets the home list render the meaningful name instead of
the autogenerated `u/{user}/draft_{uuid}` URL path. Omitted
when unchanged.

draft_users.description:
Workspace users (including the authed user, and the legacy
NULL-email row if any) who have a per-user draft at this
path. Drives the home page's user-avatar circles inside the
Draft badge. Omitted when no drafts exist.

inherited_labels.description: Labels inherited from the parent folder, computed at read time. Read-only — edit them on the folder.
Labels inherited from the parent folder, computed at read time. Read-only — edit them on the folder.

path.description: Where the app now lives, which differs from the request path on a rename.

AppDeployed.description: What a deploy of an existing app answers with. `version` is the one this call wrote, which is what an editor pins as the fork base of the draft it starts next: reading the head back afterwards cannot tell it from a deploy that landed beside it. A metadata-only update writes none and reports the head it kept.

token.description: Scoped token for the app. For sandboxed low-code apps this is the embed token handed to the opaque iframe. For a raw app it is the viewer-scoped frontend SDK token, returned only when the app is sandboxed, its policy declares frontend_sdk_scopes, and the request carries sdk_consent=true. Absent for anonymous viewers and whenever no token is needed.

raw_app.description: Raw apps render single-iframe and skip the opaque-viewer indirection and the embed token entirely. A sandboxed one may still carry a token here: the viewer-scoped frontend SDK token, which is a different credential from the low-code embed token.

sandbox.description: Publisher opted this app into sandbox isolation. When false the viewer runs the app same-origin with its full session.

app_path.description: The resolved app path; the embedder uses it to scope the app's backing localStorage per app.

workspace_id.description: The resolved workspace; pairs with app_path so apps at the same path in different workspaces don't share a localStorage store.

sdk_scopes.description: Sandboxed raw apps: scopes the app policy declares for the frontend SDK token. Null when the app is unsandboxed, however the policy reads. The viewer renders these in the permission prompt; token stays absent until the endpoint is re-called with sdk_consent=true.

viewer_email.description: The caller's own email, returned alongside sdk_scopes so the viewer can key its stored "do not ask again" per person.

DbtWarehouses.description: Warehouses a dbt project may run against, by name. `main` is the one a project gets when its descriptor names none. Each entry points at a resource; it never holds credentials.

value.description: the resolved resource, rendered into profiles.yml

resource_type.description: decides whether the value is translated into a profiles.yml target or already is one

schemas.description: the schemas its `-- schemas` annotation declares; absent when it applies to the whole database

blocked_by.description: when not run, the earliest pending migration that must be applied first; when run, the latest applied migration that must be rolled back first

instance.description: on the instance database, the only kind that can be under roles or have its access edited

usable_roles.description: the roles the caller may connect as, by name; empty when not under roles

can_create_schema.description: whether the role the listing connected as may create schemas

creatable_schemas.description: the schemas the role the listing connected as may create in

migrations_enabled.description: whether its schema is kept as versioned migrations, which a change made with plain SQL would bypass

entrypoint_function.description: Name of the function to execute for dynamic select

prefix.description: Full key prefix of the folder, ending with '/'

name.description: Last path segment, without the trailing '/'

base_url.description: root URL of the remote Windmill instance, without /api

workspace_id.description: workspace on the remote instance that deploys land in

remote_email.description: identity the stored token has on the remote instance

open_pr_error.description: server-owned, last failure opening a PR for a deploy branch of this repo

rotatable.description: whether this workspace renews the credential itself

GitCredentialStatus.description: server-owned, what the repo's own credential reports about itself

path_with_namespace.description: nested group path plus project name, which is also GitLab's project id

GitlabProject.description: a GitLab project a token can sync, as the resource form needs it

enabled_by.description: Email of the admin automatic pulls apply changes as. Set by the server when the settings are saved.

omitted_obscured_jobs.description: Obscured jobs omitted for security because of too specific filtering

InstanceConfig.description: Unified instance configuration combining global settings and worker group configs

ts.description: timestamp of the log line itself, not of the file containing it

target.description: the tracing target that emitted the line

file_path.description: the log file the line came from

line_no.description: offset of the line within its file

id.description: Unique identifier for the alert

message.description: The message content of the alert

created_at.description: Time when the alert was created

acknowledged.description: Acknowledgment status of the alert, can be true, false, or null if not set

workspace_id.description: Workspace id if the alert is in the scope of a workspace

assets.description: Whether operators can view assets

audit_logs.description: Whether operators can view audit logs

groups.description: Whether operators can view groups page

folders.description: Whether operators can view folders page

workers.description: Whether operators can view workers page

builder_flows.description: Whether operators can compose flows out of existing runnables (consumes a full seat). Omitting the field leaves the stored value unchanged.

builder_apps.description: Whether operators can compose full-code apps out of existing runnables (consumes a full seat). Omitting the field leaves the stored value unchanged.

manage_schedules.description: Whether operators can create, edit and delete schedules. Granted unless withdrawn; omitting the field leaves the stored value unchanged.

manage_triggers.description: Whether operators can create, edit and delete triggers. Granted unless withdrawn; omitting the field leaves the stored value unchanged.

AuthorLevel.description: How much of a kind of runnable a role may author. `compose` assembles already-deployed runnables with no code of one's own.

RoleVisibility.description: Pages a role sees. Not enforced.

code.description: Author scripts and run code of one's own (previews, dependency jobs, dynamic selects, resolving jobs, data table migrations). Required by `full` flows or apps.

RoleCapabilitiesPatch.description: A partial RoleCapabilities; an unset key falls through to the layer below.

RoleDefinition.description: One entry of the `workspace_roles` instance setting.

RoleOverrides.description: A workspace's overrides keyed by role name; a name the instance does not define adds a workspace-only role (EE).

custom_roles_enabled.description: Whether this workspace may add roles of its own.

all_ahead_items_visible.description: All items with changes ahead are visible by the user of the request.

all_behind_items_visible.description: All items with changes behind are visible by the user of the request.

skipped_comparison.description: Whether the comparison was skipped. This happens with old forks that where not being kept track of

diffs.description: List of differences found between workspaces

DeployEventKind.description:
What a deploy event did to the path it is recorded against: `write` (the path holds an item
after the event), `delete` (it does not), or `rename_from` (the path was vacated by a rename
to another path). Create and update are not distinguished. Omitted when no such event has
been recorded for that side, which counts as no evidence.

DeployEventOrigin.description:
Who caused a deploy event: `authored` (written in that workspace by the requester) or `sync`
(applied there by a git-sync pull or a workspace-to-workspace deploy). Only an authored
removal is evidence that the workspace dropped the item on purpose. Omitted when no such
event has been recorded for that side.

SchemasWhileloopFlow.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

SchemasAiDecision.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

FlowModuleValueOneOf5.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

FlowModuleValueOneOf6.description: Conditional branching where only the first matching branch executes. Branches are evaluated in order, and the first one with a true expression runs. If no branches match, the default branch executes

FlowModuleValueOneOf10.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

AiAgentInputTransformsMemoryId.description:
String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

AiAgentInputTransformsEnabledTools.description:
Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

AiDecisionInputTransformsQuestions.description:
Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

FlowModuleToolAllOf2OneOf5.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

FlowModuleToolAllOf2OneOf10.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

The user's prompt/message to the AI agent. Supports variable interpolation with
flow.input syntax. Required unless memory is off and `previous_messages` supplies

SchemasAiAgentInputTransformsStreaming.description:
Boolean. If true, stream the AI response incrementally.
Streaming events include: token_delta, reasoning_token_delta, tool_call, tool_call_arguments, tool_execution, tool_result

SchemasAiAgentInputTransformsMemory.description: Memory configuration - can be static (MemoryConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

SchemasAiAgentInputTransformsMemoryId.description:
String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

SchemasAiAgentInputTransformsPreviousMes.description:
Array of MemoryMessage. History supplied by the flow, sent between the system prompt
and the user message. Read only while `memory` is off or absent: managed memory
ignores it, and an older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

SchemasAiAgentInputTransformsUserAttachm.description:
Array of file references (images or PDFs) for the AI agent.
Format: Array<{ bucket: string, key: string }> - S3 object references
Example: [{ bucket: 'my-bucket', key: 'documents/report.pdf' }]

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

SchemasAiAgentInputTransformsEnabledTool.description:
Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

SchemasAiAgentInputTransformsMaxCompleti.description:
Integer. Maximum number of tokens the AI will generate in its response.
Range: 1 to 4,294,967,295. Typical values: 256-4096 for most use cases.

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

SchemasAiAgentInputTransformsTemperature.description:
Float. Controls randomness/creativity of responses.
Range: 0.0 to 2.0 (provider-dependent)
- 0.0 = deterministic, focused responses
- 0.7 = balanced (common default)
- 1.0+ = more creative/random

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

SchemasAiAgentInputTransformsMaxIteratio.description:
Number. Limits how many times the agent can loop through reasoning and tool use.
Range: 1-1000.

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

SchemasAiAgentInputTransformsModel.description:
String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the model
saved on the agent for this step's runs, on the agent's own provider resource. An
empty value keeps the saved model. Set it to an expression such as
`flow_input.model` to choose the model per run.

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

SchemasAiAgentInputTransformsReasoningEf.description:
String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the reasoning
effort saved on the agent for this step's runs, as a provider-native token (e.g.
'low', 'high', 'none'). An empty value sends no effort, so the model runs at its
default. Leave the input out to keep the saved effort, which holds only while the
step runs the saved model. A step that is not linked sets both inside `provider`.

SchemasAiDecisionInputTransformsQuestion.description:
Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

FlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueOneOf5.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

FlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueOneOf10.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

FlowModuleValueOneOf9InputTransformsMemo.description:
String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

FlowModuleValueOneOf9InputTransformsEnab.description:
Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

FlowModuleValueOneOf9InputTransformsReas.description:
String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the reasoning
effort saved on the agent for this step's runs, as a provider-native token (e.g.
'low', 'high', 'none'). An empty value sends no effort, so the model runs at its
default. Leave the input out to keep the saved effort, which holds only while the
step runs the saved model. A step that is not linked sets both inside `provider`.

FlowModuleValueOneOf10InputTransformsQue.description:
Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (faster for I/O-bound operations). Use with parallelism to control concurrency

ForloopFlowModulesItemValueOneOf4.description: Executes nested modules in a loop over an iterator. Inside the loop, use 'flow_input.iter.value' to access the current iteration value, and 'flow_input.iter.index' for the index. Supports parallel execution for better performance on I/O-bound operations

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (use with caution in while loops)

ForloopFlowModulesItemValueOneOf5.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

branches.description: Array of branches to evaluate in order. The first branch with expr evaluating to true executes

default.description: Steps to execute if no branch expressions match

ForloopFlowModulesItemValueOneOf6.description: Conditional branching where only the first matching branch executes. Branches are evaluated in order, and the first one with a true expression runs. If no branches match, the default branch executes

branches.description: Array of branches that all execute (either in parallel or sequentially)

parallel.description: If true, all branches execute concurrently. If false, they execute sequentially

ForloopFlowModulesItemValueOneOf7.description: Parallel branching where all branches execute simultaneously. Unlike BranchOne, all branches run regardless of conditions. Useful for executing independent tasks concurrently

flow.description: If true, marks this as a flow identity (special handling)

ForloopFlowModulesItemValueOneOf8.description: Pass-through module that returns its input unchanged. Useful for flow structure or as a placeholder

tools.description: Array of tools the agent can use. The agent decides which tools to call based on the task

tag.description: Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the AI agent step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)

omit_output_from_conversation.description: If true, this AI agent step does not persist its assistant or tool messages to the flow conversation when chat mode is enabled.

agent.description:
Path of a reusable `ai_agent` resource (hybrid linking). When set, the agent brain
config (provider/model/system prompt/etc.) and tool set are resolved at runtime from
that resource; the module's input_transforms then only carry the flow-local inputs
(user_message, user_attachments, enabled_tools and the history inputs memory_id and previous_messages)
and, optionally, the `model` and `reasoning_effort` overrides of what the agent saved.

parallel.description: If true, the agent can execute multiple tool calls in parallel

ForloopFlowModulesItemValueOneOf9.description: AI agent step that can use tools to accomplish tasks. The agent receives inputs and can call any of its configured tools to complete the task

tag.description: Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)

ForloopFlowModulesItemValueOneOf10.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

QueuedJobRawFlowModulesItemValueOneOf5.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result
