QueuedJobRawFlowModulesItemValueOneOf10.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (use with caution in while loops)

FlowPreviewValueModulesItemValueOneOf5.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

FlowPreviewValueModulesItemValueOneOf10.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (use with caution in while loops)

SchemasFlowModuleValueComposedOneOf5.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

SchemasFlowModuleValueComposedOneOf10.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

SchemasBranchOneBranchesItemModulesItemV.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

its older part with a summary as the conversation approaches the model's context window.

String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per

SchemasFlowModuleValueOneOf9InputTransfo.description:
Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

SchemasFlowModuleValueOneOf10InputTransf.description:
Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',

AgentToolValueOneOf1AllOf2OneOf4.description: Executes nested modules in a loop over an iterator. Inside the loop, use 'flow_input.iter.value' to access the current iteration value, and 'flow_input.iter.index' for the index. Supports parallel execution for better performance on I/O-bound operations

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

AgentToolValueOneOf1AllOf2OneOf5.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

AgentToolValueOneOf1AllOf2OneOf10.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (use with caution in while loops)

SchemasAiAgentToolsItemValueOneOf1AllOf2.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

SchemasAiAgentToolsItemValueOneOf1AllOf2.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (use with caution in while loops)

SchemasFlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueO.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

branches.description: Array of branches to evaluate in order. The first branch with expr evaluating to true executes

default.description: Steps to execute if no branch expressions match

SchemasFlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueO.description: Conditional branching where only the first matching branch executes. Branches are evaluated in order, and the first one with a true expression runs. If no branches match, the default branch executes

branches.description: Array of branches that all execute (either in parallel or sequentially)

parallel.description: If true, all branches execute concurrently. If false, they execute sequentially

SchemasFlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueO.description: Parallel branching where all branches execute simultaneously. Unlike BranchOne, all branches run regardless of conditions. Useful for executing independent tasks concurrently

SchemasFlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueO.description: Pass-through module that returns its input unchanged. Useful for flow structure or as a placeholder

omit_output_from_conversation.description: If true, this AI agent step does not persist its assistant or tool messages to the flow conversation when chat mode is enabled.

config (provider/model/system prompt/etc.) and tool set are resolved at runtime from
that resource; the module's input_transforms then only carry the flow-local inputs
(user_message, user_attachments, enabled_tools and the history inputs memory_id and previous_messages)
and, optionally, the `model` and `reasoning_effort` overrides of what the agent saved.

parallel.description: If true, the agent can execute multiple tool calls in parallel

SchemasFlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueO.description: AI agent step that can use tools to accomplish tasks. The agent receives inputs and can call any of its configured tools to complete the task

tag.description: Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)

SchemasFlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueO.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

OpenFlowValueModulesItemValueOneOf9Input.description:
String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per

while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

OpenFlowValueModulesItemValueOneOf9Input.description:
Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

OpenFlowValueModulesItemValueOneOf10Inpu.description:
Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

OpenFlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueOneO.description:
String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the model
saved on the agent for this step's runs, on the agent's own provider resource. An
empty value keeps the saved model. Set it to an expression such as
`flow_input.model` to choose the model per run.

OpenFlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueOneO.description:
String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the reasoning
effort saved on the agent for this step's runs, as a provider-native token (e.g.
'low', 'high', 'none'). An empty value sends no effort, so the model runs at its
default. Leave the input out to keep the saved effort, which holds only while the
step runs the saved model. A step that is not linked sets both inside `provider`.

Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

OpenFlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueOneO.description:
Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

Memory configuration - can be static (MemoryConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

FlowValueModulesItemValueOneOf9InputTran.description:
String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

FlowValueModulesItemValueOneOf9InputTran.description:
Array of MemoryMessage. History supplied by the flow, sent between the system prompt
and the user message. Read only while `memory` is off or absent: managed memory
ignores it, and an older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

FlowValueModulesItemValueOneOf9InputTran.description:
Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

allOf.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs

FlowModuleValueComposedOneOf9InputTransf.description:
String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

FlowModuleValueComposedOneOf9InputTransf.description:
Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

FlowModuleValueComposedOneOf9InputTransf.description:
String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the reasoning
effort saved on the agent for this step's runs, as a provider-native token (e.g.

default. Leave the input out to keep the saved effort, which holds only while the

FlowModuleValueComposedOneOf10InputTrans.description:
Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

FlowModuleValueOneOf4ModulesItemValueOne.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

FlowModuleValueOneOf4ModulesItemValueOne.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

FlowModuleValueOneOf9ToolsItemValueOneOf.description: Executes nested modules in a loop over an iterator. Inside the loop, use 'flow_input.iter.value' to access the current iteration value, and 'flow_input.iter.index' for the index. Supports parallel execution for better performance on I/O-bound operations

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (use with caution in while loops)

FlowModuleValueOneOf9ToolsItemValueOneOf.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

branches.description: Array of branches to evaluate in order. The first branch with expr evaluating to true executes

default.description: Steps to execute if no branch expressions match

FlowModuleValueOneOf9ToolsItemValueOneOf.description: Conditional branching where only the first matching branch executes. Branches are evaluated in order, and the first one with a true expression runs. If no branches match, the default branch executes

branches.description: Array of branches that all execute (either in parallel or sequentially)

parallel.description: If true, all branches execute concurrently. If false, they execute sequentially

FlowModuleValueOneOf9ToolsItemValueOneOf.description: Parallel branching where all branches execute simultaneously. Unlike BranchOne, all branches run regardless of conditions. Useful for executing independent tasks concurrently

flow.description: If true, marks this as a flow identity (special handling)

FlowModuleValueOneOf9ToolsItemValueOneOf.description: Pass-through module that returns its input unchanged. Useful for flow structure or as a placeholder

tag.description: Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)

FlowModuleValueOneOf9ToolsItemValueOneOf.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

QueuedJobRawFlowModulesItemValueOneOf9In.description:
Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

QueuedJobRawFlowModulesItemValueOneOf10I.description:
Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

JobOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowModulesItemValueOn.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

JobOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowModulesItemValueOn.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

JobOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowPreprocessorModule.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (use with caution in while loops)

FlowAllOf1ValueModulesItemValueOneOf5.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

FlowAllOf1ValueModulesItemValueOneOf6.description: Conditional branching where only the first matching branch executes. Branches are evaluated in order, and the first one with a true expression runs. If no branches match, the default branch executes

branches.description: Array of branches that all execute (either in parallel or sequentially)

FlowAllOf1ValueModulesItemValueOneOf7.description: Parallel branching where all branches execute simultaneously. Unlike BranchOne, all branches run regardless of conditions. Useful for executing independent tasks concurrently

omit_output_from_conversation.description: If true, this AI agent step does not persist its assistant or tool messages to the flow conversation when chat mode is enabled.

agent.description:
Path of a reusable `ai_agent` resource (hybrid linking). When set, the agent brain
config (provider/model/system prompt/etc.) and tool set are resolved at runtime from
that resource; the module's input_transforms then only carry the flow-local inputs
(user_message, user_attachments, enabled_tools and the history inputs memory_id and previous_messages)
and, optionally, the `model` and `reasoning_effort` overrides of what the agent saved.

parallel.description: If true, the agent can execute multiple tool calls in parallel

FlowAllOf1ValueModulesItemValueOneOf9.description: AI agent step that can use tools to accomplish tasks. The agent receives inputs and can call any of its configured tools to complete the task

tag.description: Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)

FlowAllOf1ValueModulesItemValueOneOf10.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.

cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

context_length.description: Number of most recent messages to load and store. 0 turns memory off.

MemoryTransformOneOf1ValueOneOf2.description:
Keeps the most recent messages of the memory named by the run's memory id (or the step's
`memory_id`). Without a memory id the agent runs without memory.

context_window.description:
Overrides the context window looked up from the model, in tokens. Only a model
Windmill does not know needs one; those fall back to 128000.

MemoryTransformOneOf1ValueOneOf3.description:
Keeps the whole memory named by the run's memory id (or the step's `memory_id`), replacing
its older part with a summary as the conversation approaches the model's context window.
Without a memory id the agent runs without memory, and compaction bounds the run's own loop.

context_length.description: Maximum number of messages to retain in context

memory_id.description: Identifier for persistent memory across agent invocations

String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

AgentToolValueOneOf1AllOf2OneOf9InputTra.description:
Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

AgentToolValueOneOf1AllOf2OneOf10InputTr.description:
Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

SchemasFlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueO.description:
String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

SchemasFlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueO.description:
Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

SchemasFlowValuePreprocessorModuleValueO.description:
Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory

while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

FlowModuleValueOneOf4ModulesItemValueOne.description:
Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

FlowAllOf1ValueFailureModuleValueOneOf10.description:
Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

FlowAllOf1ValuePreprocessorModuleValueOn.description:
String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

FlowAllOf1ValuePreprocessorModuleValueOn.description:
Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowM.description: Executes nested modules in a loop over an iterator. Inside the loop, use 'flow_input.iter.value' to access the current iteration value, and 'flow_input.iter.index' for the index. Supports parallel execution for better performance on I/O-bound operations

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (use with caution in while loops)

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowM.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

branches.description: Array of branches to evaluate in order. The first branch with expr evaluating to true executes

default.description: Steps to execute if no branch expressions match

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowM.description: Conditional branching where only the first matching branch executes. Branches are evaluated in order, and the first one with a true expression runs. If no branches match, the default branch executes

branches.description: Array of branches that all execute (either in parallel or sequentially)

parallel.description: If true, all branches execute concurrently. If false, they execute sequentially

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowM.description: Parallel branching where all branches execute simultaneously. Unlike BranchOne, all branches run regardless of conditions. Useful for executing independent tasks concurrently

omit_output_from_conversation.description: If true, this AI agent step does not persist its assistant or tool messages to the flow conversation when chat mode is enabled.

agent.description:
Path of a reusable `ai_agent` resource (hybrid linking). When set, the agent brain
config (provider/model/system prompt/etc.) and tool set are resolved at runtime from
that resource; the module's input_transforms then only carry the flow-local inputs
(user_message, user_attachments, enabled_tools and the history inputs memory_id and previous_messages)
and, optionally, the `model` and `reasoning_effort` overrides of what the agent saved.

parallel.description: If true, the agent can execute multiple tool calls in parallel

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowM.description: AI agent step that can use tools to accomplish tasks. The agent receives inputs and can call any of its configured tools to complete the task

tag.description: Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowM.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (use with caution in while loops)

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowF.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowF.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf2AllOf1RawFlowF.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf2AllOf1RawFlowP.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

context_length.description: Number of most recent messages to load and store. 0 turns memory off.

SchemasAiAgentInputTransformsMemoryOneOf.description:
Keeps the most recent messages of the memory named by the run's memory id (or the step's
`memory_id`). Without a memory id the agent runs without memory.

context_window.description:
Overrides the context window looked up from the model, in tokens. Only a model
Windmill does not know needs one; those fall back to 128000.

SchemasAiAgentInputTransformsMemoryOneOf.description:
Keeps the whole memory named by the run's memory id (or the step's `memory_id`), replacing
its older part with a summary as the conversation approaches the model's context window.
Without a memory id the agent runs without memory, and compaction bounds the run's own loop.

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowM.description:
String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowM.description:
Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowM.description:
String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the reasoning
effort saved on the agent for this step's runs, as a provider-native token (e.g.
'low', 'high', 'none'). An empty value sends no effort, so the model runs at its
default. Leave the input out to keep the saved effort, which holds only while the
step runs the saved model. A step that is not linked sets both inside `provider`.

ExtendedJobsJobsItemOneOf1AllOf1RawFlowM.description:
Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

EvalSubjectDraft.description: The brain and tools of an agent, as the flow editor holds them. Carried by the request and present exactly when the subject kind is `agent_draft` — the edits exist only in the editor — where it is the whole definition of what ran: the run goes through the same unlinked branch of the agent executor the editor's own test uses.

AgentDraftInputTransforms.description: The agent's input transforms: provider, system prompt, output type and the rest. The message and attachments come from the case and override anything named here.

name.description: Column header. Defaults to the last segment of the path.

pass_if.description: A score at or above this counts as a pass, and the column reports a pass rate beside its mean. Applied when results are read rather than when they are produced, so moving the line re-reads every score already recorded instead of invalidating them.

path.description: The script, or the ai_agent resource used as a judge.

EvalDatasetScorersItem.description: A scorer is a column of the results table, and it is always a runnable: an ai_agent resource sent the run to grade, or a script handed the run as an argument. `id` is assigned when the scorer is added to a dataset and never reused: it is what makes a column the same column across experiments when the scorer is renamed, and a delta is only ever computed between two scores carrying the same id. A scorer sent without an id is given one.

NewEvalCaseInput.description: The inputs a standalone run feeds the agent.

path.description: Path of the ai_agent resource.

version.description: The agent's per-path version number when the run opened: how many times the resource had been saved, not a resource_version row id. For `agent` and `agent_draft` it names the configuration the run read and every case executed. For `agent_version` it is the request's own, says which version to inline, and is required.

draft_hash.description: Hash of the configuration a draft run executed, stamped server-side. A draft moves without the version moving, so this is what dates a run of one. It is also what recognises a draft run whose configuration was later deployed: when it matches the agent as deployed, the run's kind and version are rewritten to that version, once, and the hash is kept as what the resolution rests on.

EvalExperimentSubject.description: What an eval run is executed against.

name.description: What the column is called in the dataset that ran it, resolved server-side because a list of runs spanning datasets cannot hold every dataset's scorers to look it up.

pass_rate.description: The share of scored cells at or above the column's threshold, for a column that has one. Absent where the column has no threshold and the mean is the whole headline.

failed.description: How many of the run's cells the column failed on. A column that failed on all of them has no number to report and is still one of the columns that ran.

EvalExperimentScoresItem.description: One scorer's headline for one run: the two numbers a column reports, over that run's cells.

ExperimentRowInput.description: The inputs a standalone run feeds the agent.

not_applicable.description: The scorer read this case and had nothing to measure on it. Left out of the column's mean and pass rate rather than counted as a zero.

pending.description: A scoring job is still running for this cell.

passed.description: Which side of the scorer's `pass_if` threshold the score fell on. Absent when the column has no threshold, or has no score yet.

baseline.description: The same scorer's number on the baseline experiment.

definition_changed.description: The baseline's score came from a different definition of this scorer, so the delta is a change of scorer as much as a change of agent.

ExperimentRowScoresItem.description: One scorer's verdict on one run, and how it compares with the baseline.

sandbox.description: Publisher opt-in to app sandbox isolation (alpha). When true the app is isolated from each viewer's Windmill session. When false/absent the app runs same-origin with the viewer's full session (the default, pre-isolation behavior).

frontend_sdk_scopes.description: Raw apps: author-declared scopes for the frontend SDK token. Takes effect only when `sandbox` is also true — an unsandboxed bundle runs with the viewer's own session, so no token is advertised or minted for it and this list stays inert. On a sandboxed app a non-empty list lets viewers mint (after consenting) a short-lived token carrying their own identity restricted to these scopes, handed to the app bundle so `windmill-client` calls run as the viewer. Must be a subset of the server's curated allowlist (jobs:run, jobs:read, users:read, resources:read, variables:read, flow_conversations:read, flow_conversations:write). Every such token can call whoami without consent, whether `users:read` is declared or not.

materialize_strategy.description: The Windmill write strategy it maps to, absent for `view` and `ephemeral`, which have none.

column_schema.description: Every column of the relation, typed and in the order the model produces them, from the engine's static analysis. Present only for a project that opted into it, and gated like `columns` and the model's SQL: a full column list is the shape of what the author wrote.

raw_code.description: The model's SQL as written, at the deploy this graph belongs to. Omitted when the caller cannot read the script.

original_file_path.description: Its path inside the dbt project, e.g. `models/staging/stg_orders.sql`.

AssetGraphAssetsItemDbt.description: What dbt says about the model, snapshot, seed or source that produces (or, for a source, is read at) this relation. A dbt project is one runnable node with many model assets, so per-model metadata belongs here rather than on the script.

AssetGraphRunnablesItemDbt.description: Set on a `dbt` script, which owns a whole project rather than a single output. Omitted otherwise.

id.description: Unique identifier for this step. Used to reference results via 'results.step_id'. Must be a valid identifier (alphanumeric, underscore, hyphen)

cache_ttl.description: Cache duration in seconds for this step's results

delete_after_secs.description: If set, delete the step's args, result and logs after this many seconds following job completion

summary.description: Short description of what this step does

priority.description: Execution priority for this step (higher numbers run first)

continue_on_error.description: If true, flow continues even if this step fails

job_token_scopes.description: Scopes the token of this step's jobs is restricted to (domain:action[:resource], e.g. oidc:write), on top of the flow's own restriction: a step can only narrow it. Applies to everything the step runs (loop and branch bodies, AI agent tools).

OpenFlowValueGroupsItem.description: A semantic group of flow modules for organizational purposes. Does not affect execution — modules remain in their original position in the flow. kind.description: TABLE, SEQUENCE, FUNCTION, PROCEDURE or TYPE — what the object is. A revoke turns it into the keyword it takes, ROUTINE for both routine kinds; a type's grants are read only.

args.description: identity arguments of a routine, which is what tells two of the same name apart

privileges.description: what role gave of the grant's privileges. A revoke is held back only by a source out of reach that gave some of what it takes back.

reachable.description: whether the data table's connection can take back what role gave. On an object that is the owner, when the connection acts for the owner, and otherwise the connection itself; for a default privilege, a creating role the connection acts for. What a source out of reach gave is not revocable from here; privileges only other sources gave still are.

error_message.description: Custom error message when stopping with an error. Mutually exclusive with skip_if_stopped. If set to a non-empty string, the flow stops with this error. If empty string, a default error message is used. If null or omitted, no error is raised.

error_include_result.description: When stopping with an error (error_message set), embed the stopping step's own result inside the raised error object (as error.result) instead of discarding it. The top-level result stays { error }. Defaults to false.

FlowModuleValueOneOf9ToolsItemValueOneOf.description: Early termination condition for a module

expr.description: JavaScript expression that returns true to skip. Can use 'flow_input' or 'results.<step_id>'

FlowModuleValueOneOf9ToolsItemValueOneOf.description: Conditionally skip this step based on previous results or flow inputs

enabled.description: If true, return mock value instead of executing

FlowModuleValueOneOf9ToolsItemValueOneOf.description: Mock configuration for testing without executing the actual step

required_events.description: Number of approvals required before continuing

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds before auto-continuing or canceling

user_auth_required.description: If true, only authenticated users can approve

self_approval_disabled.description: If true, the user who started the flow cannot approve

hide_cancel.description: If true, hide the cancel button on the approval form

continue_on_disapprove_timeout.description: If true, continue flow on timeout instead of canceling

debounce_delay_s.description: Delay in seconds to debounce this step's executions across flow runs

debounce_args_to_accumulate.description: Array-type arguments to accumulate across debounced executions

max_total_debouncing_time.description: Maximum total time in seconds before forced execution

max_total_debounces_amount.description: Maximum number of debounces before forced execution

allowed_origins.description: Origins allowed to call this route cross-origin, matched against the request's Origin header (ignoring case) and echoed back on a match. When set, the list governs both the preflight and the response, overriding any Access-Control-Allow-Origin the runnable returns via wm_headers. Use ['*'] to opt out of any restriction, including the http_route_default_allowed_origins instance setting. An empty list is not a configuration and resolves exactly as null does. When null, the instance setting applies, or Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * if it is unset. Ignored on a static website, which has no authentication of its own and so hands out public files: restricting which browsers may read them protects nothing while breaking cross-origin webfonts and fetches. A single-file static asset is not exempt, since it can carry an authentication_method.

macro_edges.description: Macro-library → consumer edges (deploy-recorded call detection plus `// use`). Omitted when empty.

test_edges.description: Ordering-only "must-run-after" edges — a `// data_test relationships` (or custom test reading a pipeline asset) requires the referenced asset's producer to run before the tested script. Not a data-consumption edge; fed into the cascade topo-sort so cold runs order correctly. Omitted when empty.

dbt_edges.description: `ref()` lineage BETWEEN two dbt models, in the terms the canvas draws — the relations, not dbt's node ids. Without it every model hangs off the one dbt runnable and the project reads as a flat fan-out. Omitted when empty.

dbt_snapshot_job.description: The job whose own snapshot the dbt half was resolved from, when one was asked for and found. A run page polls the graph while its job runs, because a dynamic descriptor's snapshot is written mid-run, and this is what tells it to stop. Omitted when the answer came from the version's deployed graph.

dbt_graph_ingested_at.description: When the dbt half on screen was parsed, for a graph pinned to a job. What the dbt editor labels its provenance with — "parsed from the editor at 14:32" against "as of last deploy" — since the two are drawn identically and the ambiguity would otherwise just move into the editor. Omitted for the unpinned workspace graph, which spans every project and so has no one time.

truncated.description: The component reaches further than `edges`, which holds the part nearest the asked-for relations. A trace that stops short is otherwise indistinguishable from one that ends.

GetDbtColumnLineage200Response.description: The direct column-to-column lineage the asked-for relations' columns sit in — the connected component around them — in the terms the canvas draws: relations and columns, never dbt's node ids.

test_edges.description: Ordering-only "must-run-after" edges — a `// data_test relationships` (or custom test reading a pipeline asset) requires the referenced asset's producer to run before the tested script. Not a data-consumption edge; fed into the cascade topo-sort so cold runs order correctly. Omitted when empty.

dbt_edges.description: `ref()` lineage BETWEEN two dbt models, in the terms the canvas draws — the relations, not dbt's node ids. Without it every model hangs off the one dbt runnable and the project reads as a flat fan-out. Omitted when empty.

dbt_snapshot_job.description: The job whose own snapshot the dbt half was resolved from, when one was asked for and found. A run page polls the graph while its job runs, because a dynamic descriptor's snapshot is written mid-run, and this is what tells it to stop. Omitted when the answer came from the version's deployed graph.

dbt_graph_ingested_at.description: When the dbt half on screen was parsed, for a graph pinned to a job. What the dbt editor labels its provenance with — "parsed from the editor at 14:32" against "as of last deploy" — since the two are drawn identically and the ambiguity would otherwise just move into the editor. Omitted for the unpinned workspace graph, which spans every project and so has no one time.

truncated.description: The component reaches further than `edges`, which holds the part nearest the asked-for relations. A trace that stops short is otherwise indistinguishable from one that ends.

GetDbtRunColumnLineage200Response.description: The direct column-to-column lineage the asked-for relations' columns sit in — the connected component around them — in the terms the canvas draws: relations and columns, never dbt's node ids.

truncated.description: whether the run touched more assets than are listed

producer_path.description: the pipeline script that materializes the asset (managed `// materialize` target, or a partitioned writer using the SDK helpers) — the runnable a backfill launches

GetHubFlowById200ResponseFlowValueModule.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

GetHubFlowById200ResponseFlowValueModule.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

CreateFlowRequestValueFailureModuleValue.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

CreateFlowRequestValueFailureModuleValue.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

modules.description: Steps to execute for each iteration. These can reference the iteration value via 'flow_input.iter.value'

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (faster for I/O-bound operations). Use with parallelism to control concurrency

UpdateFlowRequestValuePreprocessorModule.description: Executes nested modules in a loop over an iterator. Inside the loop, use 'flow_input.iter.value' to access the current iteration value, and 'flow_input.iter.index' for the index. Supports parallel execution for better performance on I/O-bound operations

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (use with caution in while loops)

UpdateFlowRequestValuePreprocessorModule.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

branches.description: Array of branches to evaluate in order. The first branch with expr evaluating to true executes

default.description: Steps to execute if no branch expressions match

UpdateFlowRequestValuePreprocessorModule.description: Conditional branching where only the first matching branch executes. Branches are evaluated in order, and the first one with a true expression runs. If no branches match, the default branch executes

branches.description: Array of branches that all execute (either in parallel or sequentially)

parallel.description: If true, all branches execute concurrently. If false, they execute sequentially

UpdateFlowRequestValuePreprocessorModule.description: Parallel branching where all branches execute simultaneously. Unlike BranchOne, all branches run regardless of conditions. Useful for executing independent tasks concurrently

flow.description: If true, marks this as a flow identity (special handling)

UpdateFlowRequestValuePreprocessorModule.description: Pass-through module that returns its input unchanged. Useful for flow structure or as a placeholder

tools.description: Array of tools the agent can use. The agent decides which tools to call based on the task

tag.description: Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the AI agent step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)

omit_output_from_conversation.description: If true, this AI agent step does not persist its assistant or tool messages to the flow conversation when chat mode is enabled.

agent.description:
Path of a reusable `ai_agent` resource (hybrid linking). When set, the agent brain
config (provider/model/system prompt/etc.) and tool set are resolved at runtime from
that resource; the module's input_transforms then only carry the flow-local inputs
(user_message, user_attachments, enabled_tools and the history inputs memory_id and previous_messages)
and, optionally, the `model` and `reasoning_effort` overrides of what the agent saved.

parallel.description: If true, the agent can execute multiple tool calls in parallel

tag.description: Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)

UpdateFlowRequestValuePreprocessorModule.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

RunFlowPreviewRequestValueModulesItemVal.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

RunFlowPreviewRequestValueModulesItemVal.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.
