modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (use with caution in while loops)

RunFlowPreviewAndWaitResultRequestValueF.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

RunFlowPreviewAndWaitResultRequestValueF.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

ListCompletedJobs200ResponseItemRawFlowP.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

GetCompletedJob200ResponseRawFlowModules.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

DeleteCompletedJob200ResponseRawFlowModu.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. DeleteCompletedJob200ResponseRawFlowModu.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

The user's prompt/message to the AI agent. Supports variable interpolation with
flow.input syntax. Required unless memory is off and `previous_messages` supplies
the prompt; image output always needs it.
System instructions that guide the AI's behavior, persona, and response style. Optional.

Boolean. If true, stream the AI response incrementally.
Streaming events include: token_delta, reasoning_token_delta, tool_call, tool_call_arguments, tool_execution, tool_result
Memory configuration - can be static (MemoryConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

Array of MemoryMessage. History supplied by the flow, sent between the system prompt
and the user message. Read only while `memory` is off or absent: managed memory
ignores it, and an older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

Array of file references (images or PDFs) for the AI agent.
Format: Array<{ bucket: string, key: string }> - S3 object references
Example: [{ bucket: 'my-bucket', key: 'documents/report.pdf' }]

Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

Integer. Maximum number of tokens the AI will generate in its response.
Range: 1 to 4,294,967,295. Typical values: 256-4096 for most use cases.

Float. Controls randomness/creativity of responses.
Range: 0.0 to 2.0 (provider-dependent)
- 0.0 = deterministic, focused responses
- 0.7 = balanced (common default)
- 1.0+ = more creative/random

Number. Limits how many times the agent can loop through reasoning and tool use.
Range: 1-1000.

String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the model
saved on the agent for this step's runs, on the agent's own provider resource. An
empty value keeps the saved model. Set it to an expression such as
`flow_input.model` to choose the model per run.

String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the reasoning
effort saved on the agent for this step's runs, as a provider-native token (e.g.
'low', 'high', 'none'). An empty value sends no effort, so the model runs at its
default. Leave the input out to keep the saved effort, which holds only while the
step runs the saved model. A step that is not linked sets both inside `provider`.
The implementation of a tool. Can be a flow module (script/flow) or an MCP tool reference
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Provider configuration - can be static (ProviderConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

GetJob200ResponseOneOf1RawFlowModulesIte.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

GetJob200ResponseOneOf1RawFlowModulesIte.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

is_trigger.description: If true, this script is a trigger that can start the flow

GetJob200ResponseOneOf2RawFlowPreprocess.description: Reference to an existing script by path. Use this when calling a previously saved script instead of writing inline code

path.description: Path to the flow in the workspace (e.g., 'f/flows/process_user')

GetJob200ResponseOneOf2RawFlowPreprocess.description: Reference to an existing flow by path. Use this to call another flow as a subflow

modules.description: Steps to execute for each iteration. These can reference the iteration value via 'flow_input.iter.value'

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (faster for I/O-bound operations). Use with parallelism to control concurrency

GetJob200ResponseOneOf2RawFlowPreprocess.description: Executes nested modules in a loop over an iterator. Inside the loop, use 'flow_input.iter.value' to access the current iteration value, and 'flow_input.iter.index' for the index. Supports parallel execution for better performance on I/O-bound operations

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

skip_failures.description: If true, iteration failures don't stop the loop. Failed iterations return null

parallel.description: If true, iterations run concurrently (use with caution in while loops)

GetJob200ResponseOneOf2RawFlowPreprocess.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

branches.description: Array of branches to evaluate in order. The first branch with expr evaluating to true executes

default.description: Steps to execute if no branch expressions match

GetJob200ResponseOneOf2RawFlowPreprocess.description: Conditional branching where only the first matching branch executes. Branches are evaluated in order, and the first one with a true expression runs. If no branches match, the default branch executes

branches.description: Array of branches that all execute (either in parallel or sequentially)

parallel.description: If true, all branches execute concurrently. If false, they execute sequentially

GetJob200ResponseOneOf2RawFlowPreprocess.description: Parallel branching where all branches execute simultaneously. Unlike BranchOne, all branches run regardless of conditions. Useful for executing independent tasks concurrently

flow.description: If true, marks this as a flow identity (special handling)

GetJob200ResponseOneOf2RawFlowPreprocess.description: Pass-through module that returns its input unchanged. Useful for flow structure or as a placeholder

tools.description: Array of tools the agent can use. The agent decides which tools to call based on the task

tag.description: Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the AI agent step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)

omit_output_from_conversation.description: If true, this AI agent step does not persist its assistant or tool messages to the flow conversation when chat mode is enabled.

agent.description:
Path of a reusable `ai_agent` resource (hybrid linking). When set, the agent brain
config (provider/model/system prompt/etc.) and tool set are resolved at runtime from
that resource; the module's input_transforms then only carry the flow-local inputs
(user_message, user_attachments, enabled_tools and the history inputs memory_id and previous_messages)
and, optionally, the `model` and `reasoning_effort` overrides of what the agent saved.

parallel.description: If true, the agent can execute multiple tool calls in parallel

GetJob200ResponseOneOf2RawFlowPreprocess.description: AI agent step that can use tools to accomplish tasks. The agent receives inputs and can call any of its configured tools to complete the task

tag.description: Worker group tag for execution routing. If not set, the step runs on the flow's tag (default `flow`)

GetJob200ResponseOneOf2RawFlowPreprocess.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

Provider configuration - can be static (ProviderConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

Output format type.
Valid values: 'text' (default) - plain text response, 'image' - image generation

The user's prompt/message to the AI agent. Supports variable interpolation with
flow.input syntax. Required unless memory is off and `previous_messages` supplies
the prompt; image output always needs it.
System instructions that guide the AI's behavior, persona, and response style. Optional.

Boolean. If true, stream the AI response incrementally.
Streaming events include: token_delta, reasoning_token_delta, tool_call, tool_call_arguments, tool_execution, tool_result
Memory configuration - can be static (MemoryConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

Array of MemoryMessage. History supplied by the flow, sent between the system prompt
and the user message. Read only while `memory` is off or absent: managed memory
ignores it, and an older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

Array of file references (images or PDFs) for the AI agent.
Format: Array<{ bucket: string, key: string }> - S3 object references
Example: [{ bucket: 'my-bucket', key: 'documents/report.pdf' }]

Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

Integer. Maximum number of tokens the AI will generate in its response.
Range: 1 to 4,294,967,295. Typical values: 256-4096 for most use cases.

Float. Controls randomness/creativity of responses.
Range: 0.0 to 2.0 (provider-dependent)
- 0.0 = deterministic, focused responses
- 0.7 = balanced (common default)
- 1.0+ = more creative/random

Number. Limits how many times the agent can loop through reasoning and tool use.
Range: 1-1000.

String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the model
saved on the agent for this step's runs, on the agent's own provider resource. An
empty value keeps the saved model. Set it to an expression such as
`flow_input.model` to choose the model per run.

String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the reasoning
effort saved on the agent for this step's runs, as a provider-native token (e.g.
'low', 'high', 'none'). An empty value sends no effort, so the model runs at its
default. Leave the input out to keep the saved effort, which holds only while the
step runs the saved model. A step that is not linked sets both inside `provider`.
The implementation of a tool. Can be a flow module (script/flow) or an MCP tool reference
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Provider configuration - can be static (ProviderConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

ListJobs200ResponseItemOneOf1RawFlowModu.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

ListJobs200ResponseItemOneOf1RawFlowModu.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Provider configuration - can be static (ProviderConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

Output format type.
Valid values: 'text' (default) - plain text response, 'image' - image generation

The user's prompt/message to the AI agent. Supports variable interpolation with
flow.input syntax. Required unless memory is off and `previous_messages` supplies
the prompt; image output always needs it.
System instructions that guide the AI's behavior, persona, and response style. Optional.

Boolean. If true, stream the AI response incrementally.
Streaming events include: token_delta, reasoning_token_delta, tool_call, tool_call_arguments, tool_execution, tool_result
Memory configuration - can be static (MemoryConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

Array of MemoryMessage. History supplied by the flow, sent between the system prompt
and the user message. Read only while `memory` is off or absent: managed memory
ignores it, and an older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

Array of file references (images or PDFs) for the AI agent.
Format: Array<{ bucket: string, key: string }> - S3 object references
Example: [{ bucket: 'my-bucket', key: 'documents/report.pdf' }]

Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

Integer. Maximum number of tokens the AI will generate in its response.
Range: 1 to 4,294,967,295. Typical values: 256-4096 for most use cases.

Float. Controls randomness/creativity of responses.
Range: 0.0 to 2.0 (provider-dependent)
- 0.0 = deterministic, focused responses
- 0.7 = balanced (common default)
- 1.0+ = more creative/random

Number. Limits how many times the agent can loop through reasoning and tool use.
Range: 1-1000.

String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the model
saved on the agent for this step's runs, on the agent's own provider resource. An
empty value keeps the saved model. Set it to an expression such as
`flow_input.model` to choose the model per run.

String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the reasoning
effort saved on the agent for this step's runs, as a provider-native token (e.g.
'low', 'high', 'none'). An empty value sends no effort, so the model runs at its
default. Leave the input out to keep the saved effort, which holds only while the
step runs the saved model. A step that is not linked sets both inside `provider`.
The implementation of a tool. Can be a flow module (script/flow) or an MCP tool reference
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Provider configuration - can be static (ProviderConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)

modules.description: Steps to execute in each iteration

GetSuspendedJobFlow200ResponseJobOneOf1R.description: Executes nested modules repeatedly until stopped. The implicit iterator is the iteration counter, so 'flow_input.iter.value' equals 'flow_input.iter.index' (0, 1, 2, ...) and never carries state. To carry state across iterations, a step reads its own previous-iteration result via 'results.<its_own_id>' with a first-iteration fallback - the loop's stop_after_if must then be on that inner step (a plain single-step body with stop_after_if on the loop module does not resolve 'results' across iterations and never terminates); plain counters can instead be derived from 'flow_input.iter.index', which works in every configuration. stop_after_if is evaluated after each iteration - on the loop module 'result' is the last iteration's result

GetSuspendedJobFlow200ResponseJobOneOf1R.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

GetSuspendedJobFlow200ResponseJobOneOf1R.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

ListExtendedJobs200ResponseJobsItemOneOf.description:
AI decision step: one call to a decision model (TypeSafe's Jev, Cloudflare's
Jev-compatible Clef, or OpenAI's Decisions API) that answers typed questions about a
state with calibrated probabilities, instead of generating text.
Prefer it over an AI agent to classify, route, score or check something: it is fast,
cheap and its answers are structured. Its result is { output: { <question name>: answer },
model, usage }, so a later step reads e.g. results.<id>.output.intent.choice. To route on
the answers, follow it with a branchone whose branch exprs read
results.<id>.output.<question>.choice. Usable as an AI agent tool, where the calling agent
supplies the state.

ListJobs200ResponseItemOneOf1RawFlowModu.description: Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Provider configuration - can be static (ProviderConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

Output format type.
Valid values: 'text' (default) - plain text response, 'image' - image generation

The user's prompt/message to the AI agent. Supports variable interpolation with
flow.input syntax. Required unless memory is off and `previous_messages` supplies
the prompt; image output always needs it.
System instructions that guide the AI's behavior, persona, and response style. Optional.

Boolean. If true, stream the AI response incrementally.
Streaming events include: token_delta, reasoning_token_delta, tool_call, tool_call_arguments, tool_execution, tool_result
Memory configuration - can be static (MemoryConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

Array of MemoryMessage. History supplied by the flow, sent between the system prompt
and the user message. Read only while `memory` is off or absent: managed memory
ignores it, and an older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

Array of file references (images or PDFs) for the AI agent.
Format: Array<{ bucket: string, key: string }> - S3 object references
Example: [{ bucket: 'my-bucket', key: 'documents/report.pdf' }]

Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

Integer. Maximum number of tokens the AI will generate in its response.
Range: 1 to 4,294,967,295. Typical values: 256-4096 for most use cases.

Float. Controls randomness/creativity of responses.
Range: 0.0 to 2.0 (provider-dependent)
- 0.0 = deterministic, focused responses
- 0.7 = balanced (common default)
- 1.0+ = more creative/random

Number. Limits how many times the agent can loop through reasoning and tool use.
Range: 1-1000.

String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the model
saved on the agent for this step's runs, on the agent's own provider resource. An
empty value keeps the saved model. Set it to an expression such as
`flow_input.model` to choose the model per run.

String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the reasoning
effort saved on the agent for this step's runs, as a provider-native token (e.g.
'low', 'high', 'none'). An empty value sends no effort, so the model runs at its
default. Leave the input out to keep the saved effort, which holds only while the
step runs the saved model. A step that is not linked sets both inside `provider`.
The implementation of a tool. Can be a flow module (script/flow) or an MCP tool reference
Maps input parameters for a step. Can be a static value or a JavaScript expression that references previous results or flow inputs
Provider configuration - can be static (ProviderConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run

while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an

Array of file references (images or PDFs) for the AI agent.

Example: [{ bucket: 'my-bucket', key: 'documents/report.pdf' }]

Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),

Provider configuration - can be static (ProviderConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

Output format type.
Valid values: 'text' (default) - plain text response, 'image' - image generation

The user's prompt/message to the AI agent. Supports variable interpolation with
flow.input syntax. Required unless memory is off and `previous_messages` supplies
the prompt; image output always needs it.
System instructions that guide the AI's behavior, persona, and response style. Optional.

Boolean. If true, stream the AI response incrementally.
Streaming events include: token_delta, reasoning_token_delta, tool_call, tool_call_arguments, tool_execution, tool_result
Memory configuration - can be static (MemoryConfig), JavaScript expression, or AI-determined

String. Names the memory this step reads and writes, overriding the memory id the run
was started with (the chat conversation, an app chat session or the `memory_id` run
parameter). Leave unset to use the run's memory id. A fixed value shares one memory
across every run; an expression such as `flow_input.customer_id` keeps one memory per
key. When it evaluates to an empty value the agent runs without memory. Read only
while `memory` is `window` or `compaction`: it is ignored when memory is off, and an
older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

Array of MemoryMessage. History supplied by the flow, sent between the system prompt
and the user message. Read only while `memory` is off or absent: managed memory
ignores it, and an older `auto` or `manual` memory reads neither history input.

Array of file references (images or PDFs) for the AI agent.
Format: Array<{ bucket: string, key: string }> - S3 object references
Example: [{ bucket: 'my-bucket', key: 'documents/report.pdf' }]

Array of strings naming which of the tools configured in `tools` the agent may call
this run. Leaving it unset carries every one of them; an empty array carries none.
A tool is named as the model is shown it. An entry the model is shown nothing of is
named by what identifies it instead: an MCP server by its resource path, carrying
every tool it exposes (which of them stays that entry's include_tools/exclude_tools),
and a websearch entry by the reserved name '__wm_web_search', whatever summary it carries
(no tool may take that name).
Example: ['get_user', 'u/admin/github_mcp', '__wm_web_search']

Integer. Maximum number of tokens the AI will generate in its response.
Range: 1 to 4,294,967,295. Typical values: 256-4096 for most use cases.

Float. Controls randomness/creativity of responses.
Range: 0.0 to 2.0 (provider-dependent)
- 0.0 = deterministic, focused responses
- 0.7 = balanced (common default)
- 1.0+ = more creative/random

Number. Limits how many times the agent can loop through reasoning and tool use.
Range: 1-1000.

String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the model
saved on the agent for this step's runs, on the agent's own provider resource. An
empty value keeps the saved model. Set it to an expression such as
`flow_input.model` to choose the model per run.

String. Only on a step linked to a saved agent (see `agent`): replaces the reasoning
effort saved on the agent for this step's runs, as a provider-native token (e.g.
'low', 'high', 'none'). An empty value sends no effort, so the model runs at its
default. Leave the input out to keep the saved effort, which holds only while the
step runs the saved model. A step that is not linked sets both inside `provider`.

Object mapping each question name to { type, instructions, criteria }, where type is:
- 'choice': criteria maps each option to its description (up to 255); the answer
  has choice, probabilities and confidence
- 'score': criteria is an ordered array of 2 to 10 level descriptions; the answer
  has score, legend, probabilities and confidence
- 'noul': yes/no, criteria optionally { true, false } descriptions; the answer has
  noul, the probability of yes (0 to 1)
Example: { intent: { type: 'choice', instructions: 'What does the customer want?',
criteria: { refund: 'Money back', bug: 'Something is broken' } } }

GetCompletedJob200ResponseRawFlowPreproc.description: No conversation memory/context

context_length.description: Number of most recent messages to load and store. 0 turns memory off.

GetCompletedJob200ResponseRawFlowPreproc.description:
Keeps the most recent messages of the memory named by the run's memory id (or the step's
`memory_id`). Without a memory id the agent runs without memory.

context_window.description:
Overrides the context window looked up from the model, in tokens. Only a model
Windmill does not know needs one; those fall back to 128000.

GetCompletedJob200ResponseRawFlowPreproc.description:
Keeps the whole memory named by the run's memory id (or the step's `memory_id`), replacing
its older part with a summary as the conversation approaches the model's context window.
Without a memory id the agent runs without memory, and compaction bounds the run's own loop.

context_length.description: Maximum number of messages to retain in context

memory_id.description: Identifier for persistent memory across agent invocations

frontend_sdk_scopes.description: Raw apps: author-declared scopes for the frontend SDK token. Takes effect only when `sandbox` is also true — an unsandboxed bundle runs with the viewer's own session, so no token is advertised or minted for it and this list stays inert. On a sandboxed app a non-empty list lets viewers mint (after consenting) a short-lived token carrying their own identity restricted to these scopes, handed to the app bundle so `windmill-client` calls run as the viewer. Must be a subset of the server's curated allowlist (jobs:run, jobs:read, users:read, resources:read, variables:read, flow_conversations:read, flow_conversations:write). Every such token can call whoami without consent, whether `users:read` is declared or not.

inherited_labels.description: Labels inherited from the parent folder, computed at read time. Read-only — edit them on the folder.

reported_cost_nano_usd.description: only set by providers that bill back an exact figure

key.description: the grouped dimension's value; empty when grouping by model

epoch.description: the session's move count when this copy was pushed; of a session two workspaces list, the copy with the higher one is the later

PullAiSessionBackupsRequestResume.description: where a pull of a session that did not fit one answer whole picks up; the rest of the session follows a pull naming that session alone with this as `resume`

listing.description: a fingerprint of the session's listing; pages of one session whose fingerprints differ do not belong together

moved.description: the backup kept changing while this page was read, so it may mix two versions; the browser starts the session over

partial.description: more parts of this session follow, in this push or a later one; the session is not listed on this one. Such a part names its push (`push`), or it is refused

whole.description: a part of a push of the session whole; the head is on the part that opens it, which replaces whatever the storage holds of the session, and every piece the browser has is on one of them. An incremental part instead rides on a session the storage lists and is refused with needs_whole when it lists none

push.description: a push split over several parts names itself on each with a token the browser draws; the part that opens it unlists the session and the last part lists it again, and a later part is written only while that token is the one there (refused with needs_whole otherwise)

opens.description: this part opens the push named by `push`

epoch.description: the session's move count (its record's `moves`), kept with the marker that lists the session; an incremental part rides on the marker of the same count

needs_whole.description: nothing was written and the session must be pushed whole again; an incremental part found no listed session to ride on (the backup was removed, or a push split over parts is in progress or was abandoned), or a later part of a push split over parts found another push had superseded it

is_draft.description:
True when the authed user has a draft for this app — either no
deployed row exists at this path (draft-only) or the user has
saved a per-user draft on top of the deployed row.

draft_only.description: No deployed counterpart exists at this path — the draft is the whole item.

draft_path.description:
User-typed path the editor has staged but not yet deployed.
Sourced from the draft JSON's `draft_path` field (the editor
only writes it when the typed path differs from the deployed
one). Lets the home list render the meaningful name instead of
the autogenerated `u/{user}/draft_{uuid}` URL path. Omitted
when unchanged.

draft_users.description:
Workspace users (including the authed user, and the legacy
NULL-email row if any) who have a per-user draft at this
path. Drives the home page's user-avatar circles inside the
Draft badge. Omitted when no drafts exist.

on_behalf_of.description: The user or group the app runs as in anonymous or publisher mode (e.g. 'u/admin' or 'g/mygroup'). The authority for the app's identity.

on_behalf_of_email.description: Address of `on_behalf_of`, written through from it on every save and returned as stored. Optional; when absent it is derived from `on_behalf_of`. Sending it is optional too; it must name the same account as `on_behalf_of`, and a pair that disagrees is rejected.

sandbox.description: Publisher opt-in to app sandbox isolation (alpha). When true the app is isolated from each viewer's Windmill session. When false/absent the app runs same-origin with the viewer's full session (the default, pre-isolation behavior).

frontend_sdk_scopes.description: Raw apps: author-declared scopes for the frontend SDK token. Takes effect only when `sandbox` is also true — an unsandboxed bundle runs with the viewer's own session, so no token is advertised or minted for it and this list stays inert. On a sandboxed app a non-empty list lets viewers mint (after consenting) a short-lived token carrying their own identity restricted to these scopes, handed to the app bundle so `windmill-client` calls run as the viewer. Must be a subset of the server's curated allowlist (jobs:run, jobs:read, users:read, resources:read, variables:read, flow_conversations:read, flow_conversations:write). Every such token can call whoami without consent, whether `users:read` is declared or not.

preserve_on_behalf_of.description: When true and the caller is a member of the 'wm_deployers' group, preserves the original on_behalf_of value in the policy instead of overwriting it.

skip_draft_deletion.description: When true (set by the CLI / git sync), deploying this app does not delete an existing user draft at the same path.

on_behalf_of_email.description: Address of `on_behalf_of`, written through from it on every save and returned as stored. Optional; when absent it is derived from `on_behalf_of`. Sending it is optional too; it must name the same account as `on_behalf_of`, and a pair that disagrees is rejected.

sandbox.description: Publisher opt-in to app sandbox isolation (alpha). When true the app is isolated from each viewer's Windmill session. When false/absent the app runs same-origin with the viewer's full session (the default, pre-isolation behavior).

frontend_sdk_scopes.description: Raw apps: author-declared scopes for the frontend SDK token. Takes effect only when `sandbox` is also true — an unsandboxed bundle runs with the viewer's own session, so no token is advertised or minted for it and this list stays inert. On a sandboxed app a non-empty list lets viewers mint (after consenting) a short-lived token carrying their own identity restricted to these scopes, handed to the app bundle so `windmill-client` calls run as the viewer. Must be a subset of the server's curated allowlist (jobs:run, jobs:read, users:read, resources:read, variables:read, flow_conversations:read, flow_conversations:write). Every such token can call whoami without consent, whether `users:read` is declared or not.

Use ['*'] to opt out of any restriction, including the http_route_default_allowed_origins instance setting. An empty list is not a configuration and resolves exactly as null does. allowed_origins.description: Origins allowed to call this route cross-origin, matched against the request's Origin header (ignoring case) and echoed back on a match. When set, the list governs both the preflight and the response, overriding any Access-Control-Allow-Origin the runnable returns via wm_headers. Use ['*'] to opt out of any restriction, including the http_route_default_allowed_origins instance setting. An empty list is not a configuration and resolves exactly as null does. When null, the instance setting applies, or Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * if it is unset. Ignored on a static website, which has no authentication of its own and so hands out public files: restricting which browsers may read them protects nothing while breaking cross-origin webfonts and fetches. A single-file static asset is not exempt, since it can carry an authentication_method.

ListJobs200ResponseItemOneOf1Args.description: The arguments to pass to the script or flow

modules.description: Array of steps that execute in sequence. Each step can be a script, subflow, loop, or branch

same_worker.description: If true, all steps run on the same worker for better performance

preserve_step_tags.description: If true and the flow runs on a custom worker tag, steps that declare their own non-empty tag run on it instead of inheriting the flow tag. Steps without their own tag still inherit the flow tag.

concurrent_limit.description: Maximum number of concurrent executions of this flow

concurrency_key.description: Expression to group concurrent executions (e.g., by user ID)

concurrency_time_window_s.description: Time window in seconds for concurrent_limit

debounce_delay_s.description: Delay in seconds to debounce flow executions

debounce_key.description: Expression to group debounced executions

debounce_args_to_accumulate.description: Arguments to accumulate across debounced executions

max_total_debouncing_time.description: Maximum total time in seconds that a job can be debounced

max_total_debounces_amount.description: Maximum number of times a job can be debounced

skip_expr.description: JavaScript expression to conditionally skip the entire flow

cache_ttl.description: Cache duration in seconds for flow results

delete_after_secs.description: If set, delete the flow job's args, result and logs after this many seconds following job completion

priority.description: Execution priority (higher numbers run first)

early_return.description: Id of the step whose result a sync webhook returns as soon as that step completes, while the rest of the flow keeps running. When the step does not run, or fails while the flow has a failure module, the flow's final result is returned instead.

chat_input_enabled.description: Whether this flow accepts chat-style input

notes.description: Sticky notes attached to the flow

groups.description: Semantic groups of modules for organizational purposes

ListEvalDatasets200ResponseItemScorersIt.description: A scorer is a column of the results table, and it is always a runnable: an ai_agent resource sent the run to grade, or a script handed the run as an argument. `id` is assigned when the scorer is added to a dataset and never reused: it is what makes a column the same column across experiments when the scorer is renamed, and a delta is only ever computed between two scores carrying the same id. A scorer sent without an id is given one.

on_behalf_of.description: The user or group the app runs as in anonymous or publisher mode (e.g. 'u/admin' or 'g/mygroup'). The authority for the app's identity.

on_behalf_of_email.description: Address of `on_behalf_of`, written through from it on every save and returned as stored. Optional; when absent it is derived from `on_behalf_of`. Sending it is optional too; it must name the same account as `on_behalf_of`, and a pair that disagrees is rejected.

sandbox.description: Publisher opt-in to app sandbox isolation (alpha). When true the app is isolated from each viewer's Windmill session. When false/absent the app runs same-origin with the viewer's full session (the default, pre-isolation behavior).

frontend_sdk_scopes.description: Raw apps: author-declared scopes for the frontend SDK token. Takes effect only when `sandbox` is also true — an unsandboxed bundle runs with the viewer's own session, so no token is advertised or minted for it and this list stays inert. On a sandboxed app a non-empty list lets viewers mint (after consenting) a short-lived token carrying their own identity restricted to these scopes, handed to the app bundle so `windmill-client` calls run as the viewer. Must be a subset of the server's curated allowlist (jobs:run, jobs:read, users:read, resources:read, variables:read, flow_conversations:read, flow_conversations:write). Every such token can call whoami without consent, whether `users:read` is declared or not.

The workspace and data table that govern this one. Server-owned: written by fork creation, and carried across a settings save whatever the request says.

orphan_cleanup.description: delete orphaned files older than max(retention, 1 day) (default true)

PolicyExecutionMode.description: Who may open the app, and who its runnables execute as. Optional, and what omitting it means depends on the operation: creating an app defaults it to `publisher` (runs on behalf of the app's publisher and requires an authenticated viewer), while updating one keeps the mode the app is already deployed under. Neither `anonymous`, which makes the app publicly executable, nor `guest`, which opens it to anyone the identity provider authenticates, is ever assumed. A guest is only admitted where the workspace also has `guest_access_enabled`, which is checked when the session is minted and again on every guest request

WorkspaceItemDiffForkLastEventKind.description:
What a deploy event did to the path it is recorded against: `write` (the path holds an item
after the event), `delete` (it does not), or `rename_from` (the path was vacated by a rename
to another path). Create and update are not distinguished. Omitted when no such event has
been recorded for that side, which counts as no evidence.

WorkspaceItemDiffForkLastEventOrigin.description:
Who caused a deploy event: `authored` (written in that workspace by the requester) or `sync`
(applied there by a git-sync pull or a workspace-to-workspace deploy). Only an authored
removal is evidence that the workspace dropped the item on purpose. Omitted when no such
event has been recorded for that side.

CompareWorkspaces200ResponseDiffsItemFor.description:
What a deploy event did to the path it is recorded against: `write` (the path holds an item
after the event), `delete` (it does not), or `rename_from` (the path was vacated by a rename
to another path). Create and update are not distinguished. Omitted when no such event has
been recorded for that side, which counts as no evidence.

Who caused a deploy event: `authored` (written in that workspace by the requester) or `sync`
(applied there by a git-sync pull or a workspace-to-workspace deploy). Only an authored
removal is evidence that the workspace dropped the item on purpose. Omitted when no such
event has been recorded for that side.

Optional, and what omitting it means depends on the operation: creating an app defaults it to `publisher` (runs on behalf of the app's publisher and requires an authenticated viewer), while updating one keeps the mode the app is already deployed under. Neither `anonymous`, which makes the app publicly executable, nor `guest`, which opens it to anyone the identity provider authenticates, is ever assumed. ListAllExperiments200ResponseItemSubject.description: `agent` runs the ai_agent resource as it is deployed when the run opens, `agent_draft` the caller's unsaved edits of it as the editor holds them (carried in `draft`), and `agent_version` one past version named by `version`. The first and last are read server-side; all three are inlined into the run, so every case of a run executes one configuration: a deploy part-way through changes what the next run measures, never this one.

CreateAppRawFormDataRequestAppPolicyExec.description: Who may open the app, and who its runnables execute as. Optional, and what omitting it means depends on the operation: creating an app defaults it to `publisher` (runs on behalf of the app's publisher and requires an authenticated viewer), while updating one keeps the mode the app is already deployed under. Neither `anonymous`, which makes the app publicly executable, nor `guest`, which opens it to anyone the identity provider authenticates, is ever assumed. A guest is only admitted where the workspace also has `guest_access_enabled`, which is checked when the session is minted and again on every guest request

ListInstanceDatatableRolesClusterParamet.description: The Windmill-managed Postgres cluster a data table role is a login on: Windmill's own (behind `instance` data tables) or the external instance cluster (behind `external_instance` ones). Defaults to `instance`.

GetDraftForUserKindParameter.description:
Closed set of item kinds a user can autosave as a draft. Mirrors the
Postgres `DRAFT_KIND` enum and the backend `UserDraftItemKind`.

GetOwnDraftKindParameter.description:
Closed set of item kinds a user can autosave as a draft. Mirrors the
Postgres `DRAFT_KIND` enum and the backend `UserDraftItemKind`.

GetDraft.name: get_draft
GetDraft.description: When true, overlay the authed user's draft (if any) onto the deployed payload.

IncludeDraftOnly.name: include_draft_only
IncludeDraftOnly.description:
When true, append per-user draft rows whose path has no
deployed counterpart. Synthesized rows carry `draft_only: true`
so the home page can render a "Draft" badge. Gated to
non-operators + page 0 + no narrowing filters on the backend so
picker callers stay deployed-only and pagination stays clean.

TablePreviewS3ResourcePath.name: s3_resource_path
TablePreviewS3ResourcePath.description: Read the file from this object storage resource instead of the workspace storage.

TablePreviewCsvHasHeader.name: csv_has_header
TablePreviewCsvHasHeader.description: Whether the first CSV line names the columns. Defaults to true.

TablePreviewFilters.name: filters
TablePreviewFilters.description: JSON object, column name to filter. A number column takes an optional comparison operator and a number (`>=10`), a boolean column a boolean, and any other column a case-insensitive substring, or `=value` for an exact match. A `search_term` without a `search_col` matches any column, case-insensitively.

HubPublishFolder.name: folder
HubPublishFolder.description:
workspace folder scoping the Hub publication: a workspace can publish
one Hub project per folder and the Hub-side source key is
`{workspace}:{folder}`

GcpProjectId.name: project_id
GcpProjectId.description: GCP project to list resources from, when it is not the project of the credentials

S3Sig.name: sig
S3Sig.description: HMAC signature of a presigned S3 object (bypasses the app provenance gate)

S3Exp.name: exp
S3Exp.description: Expiry timestamp of a presigned S3 object signature

SdkConsent.name: sdk_consent
SdkConsent.description: Raw apps: the viewer confirmed the frontend-SDK permissions consent banner, so the viewer-scoped SDK token may actually be minted. Without it the response only advertises the declared sdk_scopes.

Page.name: page
Page.description: which page to return (start at 1, default 1)

PerPage.name: per_page
PerPage.description: number of items to return for a given page (default 30, max 100)

JobTriggerKind.name: trigger_kind
JobTriggerKind.description: filter by trigger kind. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'schedule,webhook') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!schedule,!webhook')

CreatedBy.name: created_by
CreatedBy.description: filter by exact matching user creator. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'alice,bob') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!alice,!bob')

Label.name: label
Label.description: filter by exact matching job label. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'deploy,release') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!deploy,!release')

Worker.name: worker
Worker.description: filter by worker this job ran on. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'worker-1,worker-2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!worker-1,!worker-2')

ParentJob.name: parent_job
ParentJob.description: The parent job that is at the origin and responsible for the execution of this script if any

CacheTtl.name: cache_ttl
CacheTtl.description: Override the cache time to live (in seconds). Can not be used to disable caching, only override with a new cache ttl

RunRetry.name: retry
RunRetry.description: JSON-encoded retry policy (same shape as a schedule's retry) re-running the job when it fails. The returned id is the first attempt's; each retry is a job of its own, recorded as a child of the first attempt. Not supported for hub scripts, with invisible_to_owner, or for a script whose preprocessor would run.

NewJobId.name: job_id
NewJobId.description: The job id to assign to the created job. if missing, job is chosen randomly using the ULID scheme. If a job id already exists in the queue or as a completed job, the request to create one will fail (Bad Request)

IncludeHeader.name: include_header
IncludeHeader.description:
List of headers's keys (separated with ',') whove value are added to the args
Header's key lowercased and '-'' replaced to '_' such that 'Content-Type' becomes the 'content_type' arg key

QueueLimit.name: queue_limit
QueueLimit.description: The maximum size of the queue for which the request would get rejected if that job would push it above that limit

Payload.name: payload
Payload.description:
The base64 encoded payload that has been encoded as a JSON. e.g how to encode such payload encodeURIComponent
`encodeURIComponent(btoa(JSON.stringify({a: 2})))`

ScriptStartPath.name: script_path_start
ScriptStartPath.description: filter by script path prefix. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'f/folder1,f/folder2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!f/folder1,!f/folder2')

SchedulePath.name: schedule_path
SchedulePath.description: mask to filter by schedule path

TriggerPath.name: trigger_path
TriggerPath.description: filter by trigger path. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'f/trigger1,f/trigger2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!f/trigger1,!f/trigger2')

ScriptExactPath.name: script_path_exact
ScriptExactPath.description: filter by exact matching script path. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'f/script1,f/script2') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!f/script1,!f/script2')

ScriptExactHash.name: script_hash
ScriptExactHash.description: mask to filter exact matching path

CreatedAfterQueue.name: created_after_queue
CreatedAfterQueue.description: filter on jobs created after X for jobs in the queue only

CreatedBeforeQueue.name: created_before_queue
CreatedBeforeQueue.description: filter on jobs created before X for jobs in the queue only

ScheduledForBeforeNow.name: scheduled_for_before_now
ScheduledForBeforeNow.description: filter on jobs scheduled_for before now (hence waitinf for a worker)

AllowWildcards.name: allow_wildcards
AllowWildcards.description: allow wildcards (*) in the filter of label, tag, worker

ArgsFilter.name: args
ArgsFilter.description: filter on jobs containing those args as a json subset (@> in postgres)

Tag.name: tag
Tag.description: filter by tag/worker group. Supports comma-separated list (e.g. 'gpu,highmem') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!gpu,!highmem')

ResultFilter.name: result
ResultFilter.description: filter on jobs containing those result as a json subset (@> in postgres)

Username.name: username
Username.description: filter on exact username of user

Operation.name: operation
Operation.description: filter on exact or prefix name of operation

ResourceName.name: resource
ResourceName.description: filter on exact or prefix name of resource

JobKinds.name: job_kinds
JobKinds.description: filter by job kind. Supports comma-separated list of values ('preview', 'script', 'dependencies', 'flow') and negation by prefixing all values with '!' (e.g. '!preview,!dependencies')
